title: Remove the Handles for the Essex Kitchen Faucet
issue_description: Refer to the following directions to remove the handles for the two handle Essex kitchen or entertainment faucet.
corrective_actions: Unscrew the screw in the center of the handle that attaches the handle to the valve stem using a Philips screwdriver, taking care to protect all finish surfaces.
Gently pull off the handle and any remaining components to expose the valve.
Set all parts aside for reuse.
The valve can now be replaced or other repairs made.
Reassemble handle parts in reverse order. Note: Remove mineral deposits with a 50/50 white vinegar and warm water solution.
text:
Remove the Handles for the Essex Kitchen Faucet

Refer to the following directions to remove the handles for the two handle Essex kitchen or entertainment faucet.

1. Unscrew the screw in the center of the handle that attaches the handle to the valve stem using a Philips screwdriver, taking care to protect all finish surfaces.

2. Gently pull off the handle and any remaining components to expose the valve.

3. Set all parts aside for reuse. 

4. The valve can now be replaced or other repairs made.

5. Reassemble handle parts in reverse order.

Note: Remove mineral deposits with a 50/50 white vinegar and warm water solution.

title: Antique Kitchen Sink Faucet - Servicing
corrective_actions: Remove the Handle
Turn off the water supply.
Apply pressure to the side of the cap to dislodge and remove it.
Remove the O-ring from the collar.
Remove the screw and washer, and lift out the lever handle.
Remove the collar by pulling it firmly upward.
Spread and remove the bushing. Remove the Spout
Unthread and remove the retaining nut.
Remove the spacer.
Lift the spout assembly off the faucet body. To ease removal, slightly twist the spout assembly as it is lifted. Remove the Diverter
Grip the diverter nut with a pliers to unthread it from the faucet body.
Pull the diverter from the faucet body.
Install the Diverter
Insert the diverter into the faucet body, rubber end first.
Thread the diverter nut into the faucet body to secure the diverter in place. Reinstall the Spout
Slide the spout assembly over the faucet body. If needed, slightly twist the spout assembly as it is installed to make sure it is fully seated.
Place the spacer in the top of the spout assembly. Install the retaining nut. Reinstall the Handle
Place the bushing over the valve stem and snap it in place.
Push the collar over the bushing, aligning the handle slot with the slot in the bushing.
Insert the lever handle into the collar and over the valve stem.
Secure the handle to the valve stem with the washer and screw.
Install the O-ring onto the top of the collar.
Reinstall the cap onto the collar. Tilt the cap to engage one side first, then fully snap it into place.
text:
Antique Kitchen Sink Faucet - Servicing

# Disassemble the Faucet

Remove the Handle
- Turn off the water supply.
- Apply pressure to the side of the cap to dislodge and remove it.
- Remove the O-ring from the collar.
- Remove the screw and washer, and lift out the lever handle.
- Remove the collar by pulling it firmly upward.
- Spread and remove the bushing.

Remove the Spout
- Unthread and remove the retaining nut.
- Remove the spacer.
- Lift the spout assembly off the faucet body. To ease removal, slightly twist the spout assembly as it is lifted.

Remove the Diverter
- Grip the diverter nut with a pliers to unthread it from the faucet body.
- Pull the diverter from the faucet body.
 
# Reassemble the Faucet

Install the Diverter
- Insert the diverter into the faucet body, rubber end first.
- Thread the diverter nut into the faucet body to secure the diverter in place.

Reinstall the Spout
- Slide the spout assembly over the faucet body. If needed, slightly twist the spout assembly as it is installed to make sure it is fully seated.
- Place the spacer in the top of the spout assembly.
Install the retaining nut.

Reinstall the Handle
- Place the bushing over the valve stem and snap it in place.
- Push the collar over the bushing, aligning the handle slot with the slot in the bushing.
- Insert the lever handle into the collar and over the valve stem.
- Secure the handle to the valve stem with the washer and screw.
- Install the O-ring onto the top of the collar.
- Reinstall the cap onto the collar. Tilt the cap to engage one side first, then fully snap it into place.

title: K-6330 ProMaster® Kitchen Sink Faucet
corrective_actions: The high-arched ProMaster pullout handspray faucet features two flow types: spray and aerated.
To switch between the flow options, rotate the sprayface at the end of the nozzle.
The lever handle is not engaged for either of the two flow options.
The lever handle on the ProMaster faucet allows increased flow or water pause, depending how far the handle is engaged.
Increased flow: the lever handle is pulled slightly inward.
Water pause: the lever handle is pulled completely in. This allows faucet movement between tasks without splashing.
text:
K-6330 ProMaster® Kitchen Sink Faucet

# Sprayhead Functions - Flow Type

- The high-arched ProMaster pullout handspray faucet features two flow types: spray and aerated.
- To switch between the flow options, rotate the sprayface at the end of the nozzle.
- The lever handle is not engaged for either of the two flow options.
 
# Handle Functions - Water Pressure

- The lever handle on the ProMaster faucet allows increased flow or water pause, depending how far the handle is engaged.
- Increased flow: the lever handle is pulled slightly inward.
- Water pause: the lever handle is pulled completely in. This allows faucet movement between tasks without splashing.

title: Extension Deep Roughing-In Kits for Faucets
issue_description:
Kohler offers Deep Roughing-In Kits for installation situations where the mounting surface is too "deep" or "thick" for standard faucet installation. Deep Roughing-In Kits are considered part of a custom installation, as the product Specification Sheet indicates the standard roughing-in dimensions.  

Current Deep Roughing-In Kit part numbers can be found on the Installation Guide and/or Specification Sheet for the faucet or valve. 

The kit numbers can also be found in the current price book, located at any Kohler distributor or retailer. All kit numbers are available for purchase on us.kohler.com.

Note: Thermostatic Valve Trims do not offer Deep Roughing-In Kits. Instead, short, medium and long stem-extensions, called K-joints, are included with the trim. There is not a longer stem-extension option.

title: HiRise K-7344 Independent Sidespray Repair
issue_description: Refer to the following procedure for resolving issues with the HiRise Independent Sidespray K-7344.
corrective_actions: Ensure the water supply is turned off to the sidespray
Remove the brass valve body from the black plastic stem by removing two thumb screws. The supply hoses do not have to be disconnected
Use a Philips screwdriver to turn the screw on top of the valve counterclockwise until it stops. Do not turn too hard, otherwise the screw will loosen, which is not needed
Turn the sidespray handle counterclockwise until it stops
With both the handle and valve screw still fully turned counterclockwise, line up the notches in the black sleeve and the black plastic stem and slide together
Reinsert the thumb screws and turn the water back on
text:
HiRise K-7344 Independent Sidespray Repair

Refer to the following procedure for resolving issues with the HiRise Independent Sidespray K-7344.

1.
Ensure the water supply is turned off to the sidespray

2.
Remove the brass valve body from the black plastic stem by removing two thumb screws. The supply hoses do not have to be disconnected 

3.
Use a Philips screwdriver to turn the screw on top of the valve counterclockwise until it stops. Do not turn too hard, otherwise the screw will loosen, which is not needed

4.
Turn the sidespray handle counterclockwise until it stops

5.
With both the handle and valve screw still fully turned counterclockwise, line up the notches in the black sleeve and the black plastic stem and slide together

6.
Reinsert the thumb screws and turn the water back on

title: Nickel Allergy
issue_description:
Some individuals have an allergic reaction if they touch or consume nickel. Nickel is a naturally occurring element and is common in many products. Nearly all plated faucets manufactured today contain nickel.

Many KOHLER faucets use nickel during the plating process. A nickel substrate is applied before the chrome plating to improve adhesion and longevity of the finish coat.

KOHLER does offer faucets that are not plated and do not have a nickel plated layer on them. Faucets with a finish code of BS or S are products of this type.

KOHLER physical vapor deposition (PVD) finishes are applied over chrome plating.

Even though the nickel plating is covered by other coatings, there is no way to be absolutely certain that direct nickel contact or consumption will not occur.

Consumers with a nickel allergy should consult their physician to discuss the risks and options of using faucets containing nickel.

title: Install a Spacer Kit for a Pull-Out Faucet
issue_description: The Spacer Kit, part number 1108711, ships as two separate pieces and needs to be assembled before it is installed.
corrective_actions: Begin by inspecting the parts to make sure they are intact and the rubber seals are not warped or deformed
Place the spacer body on a flat surface with the bottom (seal side) up
Insert the check valve with the o-ring side down
Press the check valve gently into the body of the spacer unit

Your spacer is now ready to be installed, flip the spacer over and install the spacer into your faucet with the seal side down Note: If the check valve is inserted backwards, no water will come out of the faucet
text:
Install a Spacer Kit for a Pull-Out Faucet

The Spacer Kit, part number 1108711, ships as two separate pieces and needs to be assembled before it is installed. 

1.
Begin by inspecting the parts to make sure they are intact and the rubber seals are not warped or deformed

2.
Place the spacer body on a flat surface with the bottom (seal side) up

3.
Insert the check valve with the o-ring side down

4.
Press the check valve gently into the body of the spacer unit

5.
Your spacer is now ready to be installed, flip the spacer over and install the spacer into your faucet with the seal side down

Note: If the check valve is inserted backwards, no water will come out of the faucet

title: Changing Batteries on the Malleco® and Barossa® Faucets
corrective_actions: Remove the battery holder from the mounting screw.
Disconnect the battery holder wire from the power wire on the valve box. Important: Do not use rechargeable or lithium-ion batteries.
Press the tab on the battery cover to remove. Remove the old batteries and replace with new ones. Note: Do not pinch the wires when assembling the cover.
Reinstall the cover on the battery holder.
Hang the battery holder on the mounting screw and reconnect the battery holder wire to the power wire on the valve box.
Disconnect the green wire connector from the valve box.
Slide the battery holder off the valve box. Important: Do not use rechargeable or lithium-ion batteries.
Press the tabs to remove the cover from the battery holder. Replace the old batteries with new ones. Note: Do not pinch the wires when assembling the cover.
Reinstall the cover on the battery holder.
Slide the battery holder back onto the valve box.
Reconnect the green wire connector to the valve box.
text:
Changing Batteries on the Malleco® and Barossa® Faucets

# Changing Batteries on the Malleco Faucet

- Remove the battery holder from the mounting screw.
- Disconnect the battery holder wire from the power wire on the valve box.
Important: Do not use rechargeable or lithium-ion batteries.

- Press the tab on the battery cover to remove. Remove the old batteries and replace with new ones.
Note: Do not pinch the wires when assembling the cover.

- Reinstall the cover on the battery holder.
- Hang the battery holder on the mounting screw and reconnect the battery holder wire to the power wire on the valve box.

# Changing Batteries on the Barossa Faucet

- Disconnect the green wire connector from the valve box.
- Slide the battery holder off the valve box.
Important: Do not use rechargeable or lithium-ion batteries.

- Press the tabs to remove the cover from the battery holder. Replace the old batteries with new ones.
Note: Do not pinch the wires when assembling the cover.

- Reinstall the cover on the battery holder.
- Slide the battery holder back onto the valve box.
- Reconnect the green wire connector to the valve box.

title: Karbon® Faucet - Sprayhead Disassembly
corrective_actions: Turn off the water supply.
Carefully pry off the sprayhead button from the spray control.

Simultaneously press in on the spray control and pull outward on the housing to expose the setscrew. Note: The assembly is spring loaded; hold on to the housing during this step to prevent damage and loss of parts.
Use a 5/64" hex wrench to remove the setscrew and detach the sprayhead from the faucet.
Important: Do not lose the spring located inside the housing. The spring will be loose when the sprayhead assembly is removed.
Press in the spray control to release the housing from the sprayhead assembly.
Pull the housing and sprayhead assembly apart.
Make sure the spring is in place in the housing.
Press in the spray control, and slide the housing over the sprayhead assembly so the spray control is in line with the hole in the housing.
Press inward on the end of the sprayhead, and insert the sprayhead assembly into the faucet so the indent lines up exactly with the setscrew hole.
Use a 5/64" hex wrench to reinstall and tighten the setscrew.
Press the sprayhead button onto the spray control.
Turn on the water supply.
text:
Karbon® Faucet - Sprayhead Disassembly

# Overview
Follow the steps below to remove and disassemble the Karbon kitchen or bathroom sink faucet sprayhead assembly.

Important: Retain and protect any parts that are removed during this procedure.
 
# Remove the Sprayhead

- Turn off the water supply.
- Carefully pry off the sprayhead button from the spray control.
- Simultaneously press in on the spray control and pull outward on the housing to expose the setscrew.

Note: The assembly is spring loaded; hold on to the housing during this step to prevent damage and loss of parts.

- Use a 5/64" hex wrench to remove the setscrew and detach the sprayhead from the faucet.
 
# Disassemble the Sprayhead

Important: Do not lose the spring located inside the housing. The spring will be loose when the sprayhead assembly is removed.

- Press in the spray control to release the housing from the sprayhead assembly.
- Pull the housing and sprayhead assembly apart.
 
# Reassemble and Install the Sprayhead Assembly

- Make sure the spring is in place in the housing.
- Press in the spray control, and slide the housing over the sprayhead assembly so the spray control is in line with the hole in the housing.
- Press inward on the end of the sprayhead, and insert the sprayhead assembly into the faucet so the indent lines up exactly with the setscrew hole.
- Use a 5/64" hex wrench to reinstall and tighten the setscrew.
- Press the sprayhead button onto the spray control.
- Turn on the water supply.

title: Installing the K-20852 Aquifer Filter Cartridge
corrective_actions: Replace the filter cartridges: every 6 months, when the capacity has been exceeded, or when a noticeable decrease in water flow is observed.
Turn OFF the water supply.
Position a bucket under the filtration system to catch residual water.
Turn the filter cartridge clockwise as far as possible and pull down gently to remove.
Write the installation date on the new filter cartridge label.
Remove and discard the cap from the filter cartridge.
Inspect the filter cartridge for damage.
Verify that both O-rings are present and are positioned correctly in the grooves.
Line up the filter cartridge with the filter head.
Press the filter cartridge upward and rotate 90° counterclockwise to the locked position.
Turn ON the water supply.
Check the filter cartridge connections for leaks. Repair as needed.
Run water through the faucet for 5 minutes to remove any air and carbon particles in the system.
If the tabs in the filter head are not aligned, it will prevent installation of new filter cartridge.
Reinstall the OLD filter cartridge to the filter head.
Press the OLD filter cartridge upward and rotate it clockwise as far as possible.
Remove the OLD filter cartridge.
Line up the NEW filter cartridge with the filter head.
Press the filter cartridge upward and rotate it counterclockwise 90° to the locked position.
Turn ON the water supply.
Check the filter cartridge connections for leaks. Repair as needed.
Run water through the faucet for 5 minutes to remove any air and carbon particles in the system.
text:
Installing the K-20852 Aquifer Filter Cartridge

# Remove the Existing Filter Cartridge

- Replace the filter cartridges: every 6 months, when the capacity has been exceeded, or when a noticeable decrease in water flow is observed.
- Turn OFF the water supply.
- Position a bucket under the filtration system to catch residual water.
- Turn the filter cartridge clockwise as far as possible and pull down gently to remove.
 
# Install the New Filter Cartridge

- Write the installation date on the new filter cartridge label.
- Remove and discard the cap from the filter cartridge.
- Inspect the filter cartridge for damage.
- Verify that both O-rings are present and are positioned correctly in the grooves.
- Line up the filter cartridge with the filter head.
- Press the filter cartridge upward and rotate 90° counterclockwise to the locked position.
- Turn ON the water supply.
- Check the filter cartridge connections for leaks. Repair as needed.
- Run water through the faucet for 5 minutes to remove any air and carbon particles in the system.
 
# Troubleshooting

- If the tabs in the filter head are not aligned, it will prevent installation of new filter cartridge.
- Reinstall the OLD filter cartridge to the filter head.
- Press the OLD filter cartridge upward and rotate it clockwise as far as possible.
- Remove the OLD filter cartridge.
- Line up the NEW filter cartridge with the filter head.
- Press the filter cartridge upward and rotate it counterclockwise 90° to the locked position.
- Turn ON the water supply.
- Check the filter cartridge connections for leaks. Repair as needed.
- Run water through the faucet for 5 minutes to remove any air and carbon particles in the system.

text:

title: Bridge Kitchen Sink Faucets - Diverter Replacement
corrective_actions: Remove the Spout
Turn off the water supply.
Rotate the handles to the ON position to relieve pressure. Then rotate back to the OFF position.
Using a 1/16" hex wrench, remove the two setscrews from the spout.
Pull the spout up to remove it from the adapter. Remove the Faucet Parts
Using a 3/8" hex wrench, remove the adapter from the faucet body.
Remove the bearing and nut from the adapter.
Using a needle nose pliers, grasp the fins of the diverter to pull it from the faucet body.
Install the Faucet Parts
Insert the diverter into the faucet body with the fins pointing out.
Apply lubricant to the adapter where the top and bottom edge of the bearing will be seated.
Place the bearing around the adapter.
Apply lubricant to the O-rings on the adapter. Reinstall the Spout
Insert the adapter into the faucet body, then secure with a 3/8" hex wrench.
Place the nut in the bearing. Turn the nut toward the back of the faucet.
Position the spout with the setscrew holes at the back, then slide the spout over the adapter.
Make sure the setscrew holes on the spout are aligned with the holes of the nut.
Reinstall the setscrews.
Turn on the water supply.
Rotate the handles to the ON position, then check for leaks and proper operation.
text:
Bridge Kitchen Sink Faucets - Diverter Replacement

# Disassemble the Faucet

Remove the Spout
- Turn off the water supply.
- Rotate the handles to the ON position to relieve pressure. Then rotate back to the OFF position.
- Using a 1/16" hex wrench, remove the two setscrews from the spout.
- Pull the spout up to remove it from the adapter.

Remove the Faucet Parts
- Using a 3/8" hex wrench, remove the adapter from the faucet body.
- Remove the bearing and nut from the adapter.
- Using a needle nose pliers, grasp the fins of the diverter to pull it from the faucet body.
 
# Reassemble the Faucet

Install the Faucet Parts
- Insert the diverter into the faucet body with the fins pointing out.
- Apply lubricant to the adapter where the top and bottom edge of the bearing will be seated.
- Place the bearing around the adapter.
- Apply lubricant to the O-rings on the adapter.

Reinstall the Spout
- Insert the adapter into the faucet body, then secure with a 3/8" hex wrench.
- Place the nut in the bearing. Turn the nut toward the back of the faucet.
- Position the spout with the setscrew holes at the back, then slide the spout over the adapter.
- Make sure the setscrew holes on the spout are aligned with the holes of the nut.
- Reinstall the setscrews.
- Turn on the water supply.
- Rotate the handles to the ON position, then check for leaks and proper operation.

title: Alteo® Pivoting Tissue Holder
issue_description:
The left side of the tissue holder is mounted to a swivel bracket that allows the left housing and rod to rotate from a 3 o'clock (closed) position to a 12 o'clock (open) position.
 In the closed position, the rod rests on a stop on the end of the right housing.
NOTE: The tissue holder is not designed to be mounted upside down. The rod does not have a latch and will swing open if mounted incorrectly.

---

When installed, a small gap will exist between the tissue holder housing and the wall.
 The small gap is part of the product design to allow the housing and rod to swivel without scratching or marring the wall.

Corrective Actions:

 Check that the rod is resting lightly in the stop located on the end of the right housing.
 Check the spacing between the left and right brackets.  The distance between the centerlines of the brackets should be 8-3/8" (213 mm). Immediately after installation, swivel bracket operation may be stiff. Open and close the rod several times to loosen.
 If the tissue holder is installed properly and continues to rotate stiffly, replace the swivel bracket.
text:
Alteo® Pivoting Tissue Holder

# Opening Mechanism

 The left side of the tissue holder is mounted to a swivel bracket that allows the left housing and rod to rotate from a 3 o'clock (closed) position to a 12 o'clock (open) position.
 In the closed position, the rod rests on a stop on the end of the right housing.
NOTE: The tissue holder is not designed to be mounted upside down. The rod does not have a latch and will swing open if mounted incorrectly.

---

# Gap Between the Holder and the Wall
 When installed, a small gap will exist between the tissue holder housing and the wall.
 The small gap is part of the product design to allow the housing and rod to swivel without scratching or marring the wall.

# Holder Does Not Open Smoothly

Corrective Actions:

 Check that the rod is resting lightly in the stop located on the end of the right housing.
 Check the spacing between the left and right brackets.  The distance between the centerlines of the brackets should be 8-3/8" (213 mm). Immediately after installation, swivel bracket operation may be stiff. Open and close the rod several times to loosen.
 If the tissue holder is installed properly and continues to rotate stiffly, replace the swivel bracket.

title: Aquifer® Water Filtration System
issue_description:
Replace the filter cartridges every 6 months, when the capacity has been exceeded, or when a noticeable decrease in water flow is observed.

---

Many water utilities add fluoride to their water for dental and skeletal health.
 Aquifer filters do not remove fluoride.

---

Aquifer water filters are certified by NSF International to Standard NSF/ANSI 53 for the reduction of lead.
 According to the standard, the maximum lead allowed through the filter is 0.010 mg/L.

---

Aquifer filter cartridges do not reduce Hexavalent Chromium.

---

These water filters have been tested and certified by IAPMO R&T against NSF/ANSI Standard 401 for the reduction of select pharmaceuticals.
 Select pharmaceuticals include: Phenytoin, Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Estrone, Bisphenol A, and Nonylphenol.

---

The flow rate of the single cartridge is 0.85 gal/min (3.2 l/min).

The flow rate of the cartridges is 1.7 gal/min (6.4 l/min).

The micron rating for a fluid filter indicates the ability of the filter to remove contaminants by the size of particles it is exposed to.
 The K-77687 and K-77688 Aquifer water filters have a Class I Particulate rating, which corresponds to a 0.5 micron rating.
 The Class I test measures the filter's retention of particles between 0.5 and 1 micron, with the NSF requirement being greater than 85% to be in compliance.
 Both the K-77687 and K-77688 filters have tested to 99.9% or greater.

---

Aquifer filter cartridges are made of coconut shell-based carbon.

---

When you replace a filter cartridge, invert the cartridge and let it drain for 3 days.
 After 3 days, shake the cartridge to remove as much residual water as possible.
 Place the cartridge in a plastic bag provided for this purpose, and completely seal the plastic bag.
 Take the cartridge to your nearest FedEx shipping location.
 The cartridge contents will be used as concrete fill for road and other concrete structures. The plastic housing will be recycled.

---

The K-77687 and K-77688 filter cartridges are NOT compatible with the K-200 Aquifer water filtration system.
 Order replacement filter cartridge K-20852 for your K-200 Aquifer system. Cartridge number K-20852 has replaced the K-201 and K-202 cartridges.

Write the installation date on the label.
 Remove and discard the cap from the new filter cartridge
 Inspect the filter cartridge for damage.
 Verify that both O-rings are present and positioned correctly in the grooves.
corrective_actions: The flow rate of the replacement cartridge is 1.39 gal/min (5.3 l/min). ---

Replace filter cartridges every 6 months, when the capacity has been exceeded, or when a noticeable decrease in water flow is observed. For more information about the Aquifer filtration system, visit [kohler.com/filtration](https://www.kohler.com/en/inspiration/home-water-filtration-advantages).

IMPORTANT! To avoid misalignment of the new filter, the old filter must be turned fully clockwise before removing from the filter head. Position a bucket, pan, or rag under the filtration system to catch residual water. Rotate the installed cartridge fully clockwise. Remove the filter cartridge. Discard or recycle the use filter cartridge.

IMPORTANT! The filter cartridge will only engage into the filter head one way. Do not force the components. Align the filter cartridge with the filter head. Press the filter cartridge upward, and use your hand to rotate the filter cartridge counterclockwise 90° to the locked position. Turn ON the water supply. Check the filter cartridge connections for leaks. Repair as needed. Run water through the faucet for 5 minutes to remove any air and carbon particles from the system.
text:
Aquifer® Water Filtration System

# Filter Life

 Replace the filter cartridges every 6 months, when the capacity has been exceeded, or when a noticeable decrease in water flow is observed.

---

# Fluoride
 Many water utilities add fluoride to their water for dental and skeletal health.
 Aquifer filters do not remove fluoride.

---

# Lead Reduction
 Aquifer water filters are certified by NSF International to Standard NSF/ANSI 53 for the reduction of lead.
 According to the standard, the maximum lead allowed through the filter is 0.010 mg/L.

---

# Hexavalent Chromium Reduction
 Aquifer filter cartridges do not reduce Hexavalent Chromium.

---

# Select Pharmaceutical Removal
##K-77687 and K-77688
 These water filters have been tested and certified by IAPMO R&T against NSF/ANSI Standard 401 for the reduction of select pharmaceuticals.
 Select pharmaceuticals include: Phenytoin, Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Estrone, Bisphenol A, and Nonylphenol.

---

# Flow Rates
## K-77687 (Single Cartridge)
The flow rate of the single cartridge is 0.85 gal/min (3.2 l/min).

## K-77688 (Two Cartridges)
The flow rate of the cartridges is 1.7 gal/min (6.4 l/min).

## K-20852 (Replacement Cartridge)
The flow rate of the replacement cartridge is 1.39 gal/min (5.3 l/min).

---

# Micron Rating
 The micron rating for a fluid filter indicates the ability of the filter to remove contaminants by the size of particles it is exposed to.
 The K-77687 and K-77688 Aquifer water filters have a Class I Particulate rating, which corresponds to a 0.5 micron rating.
 The Class I test measures the filter's retention of particles between 0.5 and 1 micron, with the NSF requirement being greater than 85% to be in compliance.
 Both the K-77687 and K-77688 filters have tested to 99.9% or greater.

---

# Cartridge Material
## K-77687 and K-77688
 Aquifer filter cartridges are made of coconut shell-based carbon.

---

# Recycling Old K-77687 and K-77688 Cartridges

 When you replace a filter cartridge, invert the cartridge and let it drain for 3 days.
 After 3 days, shake the cartridge to remove as much residual water as possible.
 Place the cartridge in a plastic bag provided for this purpose, and completely seal the plastic bag.
 Take the cartridge to your nearest FedEx shipping location.
 The cartridge contents will be used as concrete fill for road and other concrete structures. The plastic housing will be recycled.

---

# Cartridge Compatibility
 The K-77687 and K-77688 filter cartridges are NOT compatible with the K-200 Aquifer water filtration system.
 Order replacement filter cartridge K-20852 for your K-200 Aquifer system. Cartridge number K-20852 has replaced the K-201 and K-202 cartridges.

# Replacing the K-201 and K-202 Filters with the K-20852 Filter

Replace filter cartridges every 6 months, when the capacity has been exceeded, or when a noticeable decrease in water flow is observed. 

For more information about the Aquifer filtration system, visit [kohler.com/filtration](https://www.kohler.com/en/inspiration/home-water-filtration-advantages).

# Remove the Existing Filter Cartridge

IMPORTANT! To avoid misalignment of the new filter, the old filter must be turned fully clockwise before removing from the filter head.

 Position a bucket, pan, or rag under the filtration system to catch residual water.
 Rotate the installed cartridge fully clockwise. Remove the filter cartridge.
 Discard or recycle the use filter cartridge.

# Prepare the New Filter Cartridge

 Write the installation date on the label.
 Remove and discard the cap from the new filter cartridge
 Inspect the filter cartridge for damage.
 Verify that both O-rings are present and positioned correctly in the grooves.

# Install the New Filter Cartridge

IMPORTANT! The filter cartridge will only engage into the filter head one way. Do not force the components.

 Align the filter cartridge with the filter head.
 Press the filter cartridge upward, and use your hand to rotate the filter cartridge counterclockwise 90° to the locked position.
 Turn ON the water supply.
 Check the filter cartridge connections for leaks. Repair as needed.
 Run water through the faucet for 5 minutes to remove any air and carbon particles from the system.

title: Troubleshoot desilvering
issue_description:
Desilvering occurs when the silver backing on a mirror lifts and starts becoming worn.
 Dark spots or streaks around the edges of a mirror are a sign of desilvering.
corrective_actions: Fixing a desilvered mirror is a tedious process. Contact a glass professional in your area to resilver your mirror. Contact Kohler Co.’s Customer Care Center at 1–800–4KOHLER (1–800–456–4537) for more information. ---

💡Moisture is the main cause of mirror desilvering. Wipe down steam and water droplets from the mirror immediately. Do not spray the cleaner directly onto the mirror. Spray a towel with the cleaner, and then wipe down the mirror. Vinegar-based cleaners and cleaners containing ammonia can accelerate the desilvering process. Avoid using these cleaners on your mirror.
text:
Troubleshoot desilvering

# How to Fix Desilvering
Fixing a desilvered mirror is a tedious process. Contact a glass professional in your area to resilver your mirror.

Contact Kohler Co.’s Customer Care Center at 1–800–4KOHLER (1–800–456–4537) for more information.

---

# What is Desilvering
 Desilvering occurs when the silver backing on a mirror lifts and starts becoming worn.
 Dark spots or streaks around the edges of a mirror are a sign of desilvering.

# How to Prevent Desilvering

💡Moisture is the main cause of mirror desilvering.

 Wipe down steam and water droplets from the mirror immediately.
 Do not spray the cleaner directly onto the mirror. Spray a towel with the cleaner, and then wipe down the mirror.
 Vinegar-based cleaners and cleaners containing ammonia can accelerate the desilvering process. Avoid using these cleaners on your mirror.

title: Digital Thermostatic Valve (DTV) Systems
issue_description:
The model number and version of the valve is found on a label on the outside of the valve cover.

The K-923 Laminar bath spout is compatible with the six-port digital valve.
 Refer to the spout specification sheet for more information.

---

The part number and revision level for the DTV 1 user interface is found on a label on the back of the interface.
 To access the back of the interface, use a suction cup (part #69944) to pull the interface out of the wall sleeve.

The three versions of the DTV I user interfaces are 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0.
 For the system using both a primary and auxiliary interface, they must be the same version.
 To find the version code, turn the dial on the interface and navigate to Settings > Valve > Version.

---

The DTV II system is controlled by the K-638 media module.
 System components such as the six-port valve, lighting, and other options are connected to specific ports on the media module using cables.

In the context of building code, the plastic casings of the K-682 digital valve and K-638 media module are combustible.
 These products must be installed in accessible locations for servicing.
 The system components are rated for flammability and meet UL requirements, however they are not plenum rated.

The DTV II system provides a high voltage dimmable lighting output for direct connection to incandescent lighting.
 The maximum wattage the media module can support is 250 Watts, including incandescent lighting.
 A ThermaSol MR16 lighting fixture cannot be used with the DTV II system because the fixture is driven by a transformer.
corrective_actions: The digital six-port valve can be air tested up to 100 psi (689 kPa). Before testing, install the jumper wire to open the solenoid ports. The air test begins at the hot and cold inlets of the valve.

The media module can be connected to a switch. If the switch is plugged into a router via a LAN port, and the switch is managed, then the router can assign an IP address to a device connected to the switch.

A music player can be connected directly to a DTV II system by attaching an RCA audio cable to the "audio line in" port on the media module. To connect an iPod or MP3 player, you may need a 1/8" stereo to dual phono (RCA) plug Y-cable and a phono coupler.
text:
Digital Thermostatic Valve (DTV) Systems

# Six-Port Valve

# Model Number Location
 The model number and version of the valve is found on a label on the outside of the valve cover.

# Air Testing
 The digital six-port valve can be air tested up to 100 psi (689 kPa).
 Before testing, install the jumper wire to open the solenoid ports.
 The air test begins at the hot and cold inlets of the valve.

# Laminar Bath Spout Compatibility
 The K-923 Laminar bath spout is compatible with the six-port digital valve.
 Refer to the spout specification sheet for more information.

---

# DTV I User Interface

# Part Number Location
 The part number and revision level for the DTV 1 user interface is found on a label on the back of the interface.
 To access the back of the interface, use a suction cup (part #69944) to pull the interface out of the wall sleeve.

# Version Codes
 The three versions of the DTV I user interfaces are 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0.
 For the system using both a primary and auxiliary interface, they must be the same version.
 To find the version code, turn the dial on the interface and navigate to Settings > Valve > Version.

---

# DTV II Media Module
 The DTV II system is controlled by the K-638 media module.
 System components such as the six-port valve, lighting, and other options are connected to specific ports on the media module using cables.

# Combustibility
 In the context of building code, the plastic casings of the K-682 digital valve and K-638 media module are combustible.
 These products must be installed in accessible locations for servicing.
 The system components are rated for flammability and meet UL requirements, however they are not plenum rated.

# Connecting the Module to a Switch
 The media module can be connected to a switch.
 If the switch is plugged into a router via a LAN port, and the switch is managed, then the router can assign an IP address to a device connected to the switch.

# Lighting Compatibility
 The DTV II system provides a high voltage dimmable lighting output for direct connection to incandescent lighting.
 The maximum wattage the media module can support is 250 Watts, including incandescent lighting.
 A ThermaSol MR16 lighting fixture cannot be used with the DTV II system because the fixture is driven by a transformer.

# Connecting a Music Player
 A music player can be connected directly to a DTV II system by attaching an RCA audio cable to the "audio line in" port on the media module.
 To connect an iPod or MP3 player, you may need a 1/8" stereo to dual phono (RCA) plug Y-cable and a phono coupler.

title: Canac Kitchen Cabinetry
issue_description:
💡Unfortunately Canac no longer has any parts or service available. Please consult with a local cabinet shop for assistance with your cabinets. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause you.

KOHLER, Wisconsin - September 25, 2008 - Kohler Co. announced today that it will close its Canac kitchen cabinetry business, citing the United States' weak housing market, recent construction softness in Canada, and escalating costs for raw materials and logistics costs as the driving reasons for the business closure.

Canac has been experiencing a decline in orders for some time and competes in an already crowded and price-sensitive kitchen cabinetry marketplace that itself has been in decline. Canac's primary customers are in North America, including big builders in the new home construction market and developers in the multifamily sector. A full business closure is anticipated by year end.

"We explored all possible business options with our first preference being the sale of Canac assets to an interested buyer. However, that option never garnered any serious interest with the potential buyers," said Canac President Ralph Howard. "The last option we considered was closing the Canac business altogether, but unfortunately that is the reality we are now facing. We realize this decision impacts our associates significantly. It was a very difficult decision for us to make."

Kohler, which acquired Canac in 1996, stressed that this decision to exit the kitchen cabinetry business is based purely on the sub-par performance of its Canac business. The company's other brands participating in the housing industry, including Kohler plumbing, Sterling plumbing and Robern mirrored bathroom cabinetry, are not impacted.

1
Gelcoat material is sprayed onto a mold to provide the shape of the product.

A fiberglass and resin mix is applied to the gelcoat layer to provide strength.

3

title: Verdera™ 40" Cabinet - Shelf Installation
issue_description:
To install the shelves for the large 40" Verdera cabinets (K-99010, K-99011), door removal is required.
 To ease removal, all doors on the large cabinets are equipped with quick-release hinges.

IMPORTANT! Do not leave the door supported with only one hinge during removal or reinstallation. Disengage the bottom hinge first during removal, and reattach the top hinge first during installation.

---
corrective_actions: 1 With one hand, support the door in the open position. 2 Starting with the bottom hinge, press the latch at the end of the hinge to release it from the bracket. 3 Repeat for the upper hinge. 4 Move the door forward to slide the hinges off the brackets.

1 With one hand, support the door in the open position. 2 Starting with the top bracket, align the hinge pin with the cup of the bracket. 3 Press the back of the hinge to snap the latch onto the bracket. 4 Repeat for the lower hinge. 5 Open and close the door to ensure proper operation.
text:
Verdera™ 40" Cabinet - Shelf Installation

# Overview

 To install the shelves for the large 40" Verdera cabinets (K-99010, K-99011), door removal is required.
 To ease removal, all doors on the large cabinets are equipped with quick-release hinges.

IMPORTANT! Do not leave the door supported with only one hinge during removal or reinstallation. Disengage the bottom hinge first during removal, and reattach the top hinge first during installation.

---

# Door Removal and Reinstallation

## Remove

1
With one hand, support the door in the open position.

2
Starting with the bottom hinge, press the latch at the end of the hinge to release it from the bracket.

3
Repeat for the upper hinge.

4
Move the door forward to slide the hinges off the brackets.

## Reinstall

1
With one hand, support the door in the open position.

2
Starting with the top bracket, align the hinge pin with the cup of the bracket.

3
Press the back of the hinge to snap the latch onto the bracket.

4
Repeat for the lower hinge.

5
Open and close the door to ensure proper operation.

title: New Hinge for Kohler Cabinets
issue_description:
Kohler cabinetry upgraded hinge kits to ensure durability. The new hinges are made of all metal and no longer have plastic components as shown on the older hinges. Hinge packs and hardware kits have been upgraded to the new metal hinges.

The fingers on the new hinge are a tight fit when replacing the older style with new.

It is best to loosen the door hinge screws to give the new hinge fingers some room to maneuver. While the fit of these new hinges may be difficult on older cabinets, they will go on and are the new replacements that are available.

Hinge screw sizes:

 Hinge to Door: #6-32 x 3/8" 100 Deg Philips Head 18/8 Stainless
 Hinge to Cabinet: #8-32 x 3/8" Truss Head

Note: New cabinets are now manufactured with slightly larger slots and will not have the same issue.

title: Finding a KOHLER or STERLING Product Model Number or Serial Number
issue_description:
Click the links below to be directed to specific product model number locations.

[Identifying Your Toilet Model](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-toilet-model)

[Identifying Your DTV® and DTV Interface Model Numbers](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-dtv-and-dtv-interface-model-numbers)

[Identifying Your Faucet Model](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-faucet-model)

[Identifying Your Sink Model](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-sink-model)

[Identifying Your Mirror/Medicine Cabinet Model](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-mirror-medicine-cabinet-model)

[Identifying Your Shower Door Model](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-shower-door-model)

[Identifying Your Shower Base Model](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-shower-base-model)

[Identify a Single Control Bath/Shower Valve](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identify-a-single-control-bath-shower-valve)

[Identifying Your Steam Generator Model](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-steam-generator-model)

[Identifying Your STERLING Wall Set Model](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-sterling-wall-set-model)

[](https://kohlerpiaprod.appgw.ocpaz.mykohler.com/)

---

Model numbers for KOHLER products contain a base number, followed by a dash, and series of letters and numbers.
 KOHLER model numbers have a "K" in front of the base number. The "K" may not be included on certain product labels and when stamped onto the product itself.
 Letters or numbers following the base number represent a series, style, or variation. For example, "RA" means right-hand trip lever for a toilet, or right-hand drain for a bath.
 Letters or numbers following the series/style/variation indicate the product color or finish. For example, "0" is the color code for a white fixture such as a toilet, and "CP" signifies a polished chrome finish for a faucet.
 Letters at the end, after the color/finish, designate the product generation. A first-generation model will have "AA" and the evolution of the product will supersede as "AB" or "AC" or "BA" etc.

---

Serial numbers for KOHLER and STERLING products are usually 8 to 11 characters long, most commonly 9 characters long.
 Most serial numbers start with the letter “S” and the remaining characters will be alpha and/or numeric.
 The serial numbers for Steam Generators and DTV start with any alpha or numeric character.
 A serial number does not contain any dashes or hyphens.

---

KOHLER and STERLING product model numbers may be found in several places:

 Product label on the box in which the product was packaged
 Product literature, such as a homeowners guide, installation instructions, or specification sheet
 An invoice or receipt from the place of purchase
 Stamped directly onto the product itself

A STERLING product model number can also be identified by visiting [sterlingplumbing.com](https://www.sterlingplumbing.com/) and browsing similar products.

Product model numbers can also be determined by locating the product serial label and contacting the Customer Care Center.

issue_description: Widespread bathroom sink faucet retrofit kits do not fit on older-style handle escutcheons.
corrective_actions: Owners of pre-1992 widespread bathroom sink faucets who purchase a new retrofit kit may also need to purchase a new escutcheon or handle kit if the handle escutcheon slides over the threads instead of threading on.

Pre-1992 Widespread Faucet Retrofit Kits

Widespread bathroom sink faucet retrofit kits do not fit on older-style handle escutcheons.

title: Katun Faucet Stream Breaker Removal
issue_description:
The following directions provide information on removing the stream breaker, or aerator, for the Katun  bathroom faucet, models K-R78037-4D-, K-R78038-4D-, and K-R78039-4D-. The stream breaker is the internal “grid” piece at the end of the faucet spout.

Removal of the stream breaker may be necessary to clean any hard water build up. Clean the stream breaker with a 50/50 solution of white vinegar and warm water.
corrective_actions: Hex key wrench
Small needle nose pliers or tweezers
Use the hex key tool to remove the set screw

Use the needle nose pliers or tweezers to grip in between the “grid” squares of the stream breaker and pull straight down/out. Optional for Centerset or Single-Control faucets: use Stream Breaker Removal Tool, part number 1118166 (sold separately)

The stream breaker includes two plastic screens that sit up in the spout body and should come out when the stream breaker comes out . If they don't come out, use the needle nose pliers or tweezers to remove them
Clean the stream breaker with a 50/50 solution of white vinegar and warm water
To reinstall, align the stream breaker hole with the set screw and tighten the set screw until flush with the spout
Centerset Stream Breaker Kit – part number 1325506
Single-handle Stream Breaker Kit - part number 1325506
Widespread Stream Breaker Kit – part number 1307518
Stream Breaker Removal Tool for use with Centerset and Single-control faucets only - part number  1118166 (sold separately)
text:
Katun Faucet Stream Breaker Removal

The following directions provide information on removing the stream breaker, or aerator, for the Katun  bathroom faucet, models K-R78037-4D-, K-R78038-4D-, and K-R78039-4D-. The stream breaker is the internal “grid” piece at the end of the faucet spout.

Removal of the stream breaker may be necessary to clean any hard water build up. Clean the stream breaker with a 50/50 solution of white vinegar and warm water.

# Tools Needed:
- Hex key wrench

- Small needle nose pliers or tweezers

1. Use the hex key tool to remove the set screw

2. Use the needle nose pliers or tweezers to grip in between the “grid” squares of the stream breaker and pull straight down/out. Optional for Centerset or Single-Control faucets: use Stream Breaker Removal Tool, part number 1118166 (sold separately)

3. The stream breaker includes two plastic screens that sit up in the spout body and should come out when the stream breaker comes out . If they don't come out, use the needle nose pliers or tweezers to remove them

4. Clean the stream breaker with a 50/50 solution of white vinegar and warm water

5. To reinstall, align the stream breaker hole with the set screw and tighten the set screw until flush with the spout

# Stream Breaker Part Numbers:

- Centerset Stream Breaker Kit – part number 1325506
- Single-handle Stream Breaker Kit - part number 1325506

title: Change a Kohler Ceramic Valve Cartridge from "Hot" to "Cold"
issue_description:
Although Kohler ceramic valve cartridges are available in hot (which means the water turns off by turning the handle clockwise) and cold (the water turns off counterclockwise), the only difference between the two is the way the valves turn. However, if you mistakenly have a “hot” when you need a “cold,” the valves can be reversed.

On the top of the valve, at the base of the splined stem, there is a clip. The clip can be removed either with your fingers or needle-nose pliers. Do not lose the clip as you will need to reinstall it later.

Once the clip is removed, lift the silver disk underneath and turn it 90 degrees. Then slide the disk back down and reinstall the clip. This will allow the valve to turn in the other direction.

Note: ultra glide valves are not reversible.

Change a Kohler Ceramic Valve Cartridge from "Hot" to "Cold"

title: Replace Valvet Service Kit Instructions
issue_description: Refer to the instructions below for removal and replacement of the full turn and quarter turn valvets.
corrective_actions: Note: Now discontinued and replaced by GP330002 and GP330004 (directions below).
Turn off the water supply.
Open the valve to relieve pressure and to drain the faucet.
Remove the faucet handle.
Loosen and remove the bonnet from the faucet body. The stem o-ring and/or washer may remain within the recess in the bonnet. Remove the washer and the stem o-ring and discard.

Lift out the stem sub-assembly from the faucet body. The plunger with the seat washer attached will remain assembled to the threaded portion of the stem. The sleeve sub-assembly will remain within the faucet body.
Lift out the sleeve sub-assembly and discard.
Replace the bonnet o-ring with one of the two large o-rings. Discard the unused o-ring.

Place your current handle and bonnet assembly onto the stem assembly to make sure that the stem and plunger threads are the same as on the parts removed. Your handle should turn on and off in the same direction as the old parts. If they are the same, discard old parts. ---
Assemble all new valvet parts before inserting into the faucet body as follows:

Line up bosses on the plunger with grooves in the sleeve and insert stem assembly into the sleeve. Place the bonnet over the splined end of the stem. Move the bonnet toward the sleeve until the o-ring is fully engaged in the bonnet and the bonnet is tight against the sleeve. ---
Insert the entire valvet assembly into the faucet body.
Grip the splined end of the stem to prevent it from turning, and turn the bonnet into the faucet body.
Reinstall the handle.
Turn the handle to the off position.
Turn on the water supply.

Open the valve unit to full open and then close again. If the handle does not stop in either direction, the bonnet has not been properly tightened. Open the valve, remove the handle, and retighten the bonnet. Replace the handle. Quarter Turn Valvet GP330002 and GP330004 Replacement Instructions Note: The new quarter turn valvet GP330002 or GP330004 will now turn a quarter turn compared to the old GP30002 or GP30004. The new valve may look different but it is a direct replacement.
Turn water supply off during service.
Open the valve to relieve pressure and drain the faucet.
Remove the existing valvet.
If existing valvet is full turn, refer to the Old Valvet Removal steps above.
If existing valvet is quarter turn, remove the handle, then the bonnet, and pull out the existing valvet.
Replace the existing valvet with the new quarter turn valvet.
Tighten the bonnet and reinstall the handle.
Turn the handle to the off position.
Turn on the water supply fully and check for proper operation.
text:
Replace Valvet Service Kit Instructions

Refer to the instructions below for removal and replacement of the full turn and quarter turn valvets.

# Full Turn Valvet GP30002 and GP30004 Replacement Instructions
Note: Now discontinued and replaced by GP330002 and GP330004 (directions below).

# Old Valvet Removal

1.
Turn off the water supply.

2.
Open the valve to relieve pressure and to drain the faucet.

3.
Remove the faucet handle.

4.
Loosen and remove the bonnet from the faucet body. The stem o-ring and/or washer may remain within the recess in the bonnet. Remove the washer and the stem o-ring and discard.

5.
Lift out the stem sub-assembly from the faucet body. The plunger with the seat washer attached will remain assembled to the threaded portion of the stem. The sleeve sub-assembly will remain within the faucet body.

6.
Lift out the sleeve sub-assembly and discard.

7.
Replace the bonnet o-ring with one of the two large o-rings. Discard the unused o-ring.

8.
Place your current handle and bonnet assembly onto the stem assembly to make sure that the stem and plunger threads are the same as on the parts removed. Your handle should turn on and off in the same direction as the old parts. If they are the same, discard old parts.

---

# Valvet Assembly
1.
Assemble all new valvet parts before inserting into the faucet body as follows:

2.
Line up bosses on the plunger with grooves in the sleeve and insert stem assembly into the sleeve.
Place the bonnet over the splined end of the stem. Move the bonnet toward the sleeve until the o-ring is fully engaged in the bonnet and the bonnet is tight against the sleeve.

---

# New Valvet Installation
1.
Insert the entire valvet assembly into the faucet body.

2.
Grip the splined end of the stem to prevent it from turning, and turn the bonnet into the faucet body.

3.
Reinstall the handle.

4.
Turn the handle to the off position.

5.
Turn on the water supply.

6.
Open the valve unit to full open and then close again. If the handle does not stop in either direction, the bonnet has not been properly tightened. Open the valve, remove the handle, and retighten the bonnet. Replace the handle.

Quarter Turn Valvet GP330002 and GP330004 Replacement Instructions

Note: The new quarter turn valvet GP330002 or GP330004 will now turn a quarter turn compared to the old GP30002 or GP30004. The new valve may look different but it is a direct replacement.

1.
Turn water supply off during service.

2.
Open the valve to relieve pressure and drain the faucet.

3.
Remove the existing valvet.  
   - If existing valvet is full turn, refer to the Old Valvet Removal steps above.
   - If existing valvet is quarter turn, remove the handle, then the bonnet, and pull out the existing valvet.

4.
Replace the existing valvet with the new quarter turn valvet.

5.
Tighten the bonnet and reinstall the handle.

6.
Turn the handle to the off position.

7.
Turn on the water supply fully and check for proper operation.

title: Maxton Faucet Stream Breaker Removal
issue_description:
The following directions provide information on removing the stream breaker, or aerator, for the Maxton bathroom faucet, models K-R22475-4D-, K-R22476-4D- and K-R22477-4D-.

Removal of the stream breaker may be necessary to clean any hard water build up. Clean the stream breaker with a 50/50 solution of white vinegar and warm water.

Tool Needed:
corrective_actions: Small needle nose pliers or tweezer The stream breaker is the internal “grid” piece. The outer solid grey plastic piece will stay in place. NOTE: DO NOT REMOVE the small Philip’s head screw when pulling out the stream breaker
Use the needle nose pliers or tweezers to grip in between the “grid” squares of the stream breaker and pull straight down/out.

The stream breaker includes two plastic screens that sit up in the spout body and should come out when the stream breaker comes out. If they don't come out, use the needle nose pliers or tweezers to remove them. Stream Breaker Part Numbers:
Centerset Stream Breaker – part number 1315070

Widespread Stream Breaker – part number 1307522 Note: The centerset part number will include a Philip’s head screw. This screw will NOT need to be used when removing and installing the new stream breaker.

text:
Single-Handle Bathroom Sink Faucets - Handle Removal

- Lift off the handle.
- Unthread the bonnet to expose the valve.

- Using a bladed screwdriver, gently pry off the cap, taking care to protect all finished surfaces.
- Using a Phillips screwdriver, remove the screw that attaches the handle to the valve stem.
- Lift off the handle.
- Unthread the nut to expose the valve.

---

# Trocadero®

- Using a 3/32" hex wrench, unthread the setscrew attaching the lever to the valve stem.
- Lift off the handle, cap, and sphere to expose the valve.

---

# Falling Water®

- Using a 1/8" hex wrench, unthread the setscrew securing the handle to the valve stem.
- Remove the handle.
- Unthread the cap to expose the valve.

title: Widespread Faucet - Quick Connect Supply Tee
issue_description:
- Each hose that attaches to the tee contains two white snap connectors that interlock with the tee.
- The tee may leak if the snap connectors are not properly seated in the tee.
- Refer to the instructions below to properly connect and disconnect the supply hoses to the tee.

---
corrective_actions: Connect
Make sure the O-ring is seated onto the end of the hose as shown.
Press the white snap connectors in while inserting the end of the hose into the tee.
Push the hose and tee together until both snap connectors click into place. Disconnect

text:
Widespread Faucet - Quick Connect Supply Tee

# Overview

- Each hose that attaches to the tee contains two white snap connectors that interlock with the tee.
- The tee may leak if the snap connectors are not properly seated in the tee.
- Refer to the instructions below to properly connect and disconnect the supply hoses to the tee.

---

# Hose and Tee Connection

Connect

- Make sure the O-ring is seated onto the end of the hose as shown.
- Press the white snap connectors in while inserting the end of the hose into the tee.
- Push the hose and tee together until both snap connectors click into place.

Disconnect

- To detach the hose, press one side of the white snap connector in, and gently pull on the hose.
- The white snap connector will withdraw under the edge of the tee.
- Then press the opposite side snap connector to release the hose.

title: Remove the Handles for the Devonshire Bathroom Faucet
issue_description: To remove the handles for the Devonshire widespread or centerset bathroom faucets or bidet faucets, refer to the following directions.
corrective_actions: Hold the handle with one hand. Using your other hand, turn the skirt, the decorative flared piece below the handle, counterclockwise. A strap wrench may also be used, taking care to protect all finish surfaces.
Remove any remaining components to expose the valve. Set all parts aside for re-use.
The valve can now be replaced or other repairs made.
Reassemble handle parts in reverse order. Note: Remove mineral deposits with a 50/50 mixture of white vinegar and warm water. ---
To remove the handle for the centerset Devonshire bathroom faucet, refer to the following directions. Style 1:
Hold on to the handle while turning the skirt counterclockwise by hand or with a strap wrench, taking care to protect all finish surfaces.
Remove any remaining components to expose the valve. Set all parts aside for re-use.
The valve can now be replaced or other repairs made.
Reassemble handle parts in reverse order. Style 2
Use a 3/32" hex wrench to loosen the set screw located in the back of the lever handle.
Use a Philips screwdriver to remove the screw in the bonnet. Set all parts aside for re-use.
The valve can now be replaced or other repairs made.
Reassemble handle parts in reverse order. Note: Remove mineral deposits with a 50/50 white vinegar and warm water solution.
text:

3. The valve can now be replaced or other repairs made.

4. Reassemble handle parts in reverse order.

Note: Remove mineral deposits with a 50/50 mixture of white vinegar and warm water.

---

2. Remove any remaining components to expose the valve. Set all parts aside for re-use.

3. The valve can now be replaced or other repairs made.

4. Reassemble handle parts in reverse order.

Style 2

1. Use a 3/32" hex wrench to loosen the set screw located in the back of the lever handle.

2. Use a Philips screwdriver to remove the screw in the bonnet. Set all parts aside for re-use.

title: Handle Adjustment with Spline Adapter
issue_description: A valve cartridge stem features 20 splines, and the handle features 19 splines. Because of this, the handle can be adjusted to within less than 1/2 degree of perfect alignment. To adjust the handle alignment properly, the spline adapter must be oriented correctly between the valve and the handle.
corrective_actions: Remove the handles.

Verify that both valves are fully rotated to the OFF position. Note: The valves can rotate a few degrees before water begins to flow. Do not mistake water not flowing as an indicator that the valves are in the fully OFF position ---
Install the black plastic spline adapter onto the valve cartridge stem, with the split in the adapter as close to the 12 o’clock position as possible.
If the spline adapter slides easily over the valve cartridge stem, fully slide the adapter onto the valve stem.
If the spline adapter fits tightly onto the valve cartridge stem, partially slide the spline adapter onto the stem. ---
WARNING! Do not fully install the handle as it may get lodged in the handle splines and be difficult to remove.

With the spline adapter in place, partially install the handle onto the spline adapter to determine the closest alignment of the handle. Note: Partially installing the handle may take a couple attempts to see which spline engagement is the best.
The handle should fall within 10 degrees of the 3 o’clock or 9 o’clock position, depending on whether the handle is the cold or hot handle. ---

Once you have determined the closest fit to the 3 o’clock or 9 o’clock position, determine whether the handles need to be rotated to improve alignment. If the handle is nearly the same distance off perfect alignment from one spline engagement to the next:
Turn the spline adapter 180 degrees.
If the spline adapter split is at 12 o’clock, place the split at 6 o’clock. If the handle needs to be rotated clockwise for perfect alignment:
Remove the handle and rotate the spline adapter counterclockwise. If the handle needs to be rotated counterclockwise for perfect alignment:
Remove the handle and rotate the spline adapter clockwise.
text:
Handle Adjustment with Spline Adapter

A valve cartridge stem features 20 splines, and the handle features 19 splines. Because of this, the handle can be adjusted to within less than 1/2 degree of perfect alignment. To adjust the handle alignment properly, the spline adapter must be oriented correctly between the valve and the handle.
 
# Remove the Handles

- Remove the handles.
- Verify that both valves are fully rotated to the OFF position.

Note: The valves can rotate a few degrees before water begins to flow. Do not mistake water not flowing as an indicator that the valves are in the fully OFF position

---

# Install the Spline Adapter

- Install the black plastic spline adapter onto the valve cartridge stem, with the split in the adapter as close to the 12 o’clock position as possible.
- If the spline adapter slides easily over the valve cartridge stem, fully slide the adapter onto the valve stem.
- If the spline adapter fits tightly onto the valve cartridge stem, partially slide the spline adapter onto the stem.

---

# Partially Installing the Handles

WARNING! Do not fully install the handle as it may get lodged in the handle splines and be difficult to remove.

- With the spline adapter in place, partially install the handle onto the spline adapter to determine the closest alignment of the handle.
Note: Partially installing the handle may take a couple attempts to see which spline engagement is the best.

- The handle should fall within 10 degrees of the 3 o’clock or 9 o’clock position, depending on whether the handle is the cold or hot handle.

---

# Adjusting the Spline Adapter for Perfect Alignment of Handles
- Once you have determined the closest fit to the 3 o’clock or 9 o’clock position, determine whether the handles need to be rotated to improve alignment.

If the handle is nearly the same distance off perfect alignment from one spline engagement to the next:

- Turn the spline adapter 180 degrees.
- If the spline adapter split is at 12 o’clock, place the split at 6 o’clock.

If the handle needs to be rotated clockwise for perfect alignment:

- Remove the handle and rotate the spline adapter counterclockwise.
If the handle needs to be rotated counterclockwise for perfect alignment:

- Remove the handle and rotate the spline adapter clockwise.

title: Removing the Avid™ Single-Control Bonnet and Handle
issue_description:
The following topic covers the removal and reinstallation of the Avid single-control bonnet and handle.

---
corrective_actions: Turn the water supply OFF.
Turn the handle to the ON position to relieve pressure.
Loosen the setscrew and remove the handle.
Use a flat-blade screwdriver to lift and remove the bonnet from the faucet body.
The valve is now accessible for servicing. ---
Apply lubricant to the wall of the bonnet slot.
Verify that the O-ring is properly seated in the new bonnet.
Reinstall the bonnet by tilting the beveled end in first. Pivot and press the bonnet into place.
Install the handle and tighten the setscrew.
Turn the water supply ON.
Rotate the handle to the ON position and check for leaks.
text:
Removing the Avid™ Single-Control Bonnet and Handle

# Overview
The following topic covers the removal and reinstallation of the Avid single-control bonnet and handle.

---

# Remove the Bonnet and Handle

- Turn the water supply OFF.
- Turn the handle to the ON position to relieve pressure.
- Loosen the setscrew and remove the handle.
- Use a flat-blade screwdriver to lift and remove the bonnet from the faucet body.
- The valve is now accessible for servicing.

---

# Reinstall the Bonnet and Handle

- Apply lubricant to the wall of the bonnet slot.
- Verify that the O-ring is properly seated in the new bonnet.
- Reinstall the bonnet by tilting the beveled end in first. Pivot and press the bonnet into place.
- Install the handle and tighten the setscrew.
- Turn the water supply ON.
- Rotate the handle to the ON position and check for leaks.

title: Enameled Cast Iron Sink Care
corrective_actions: Enameled surfaces can lose the original luster with improper care and cleaning. Abrasive cleaners are not recommended.
For detailed cleaning information and products to consider, visit [kohler.com/clean](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/how-to-use-kohler-cleaning-products). ---
Rubber dish mats are not recommended in KOHLER® sinks.
Bacteria can grow under the mats and permanently discolor the enamel.
Discoloration from rubber mats is not covered under the manufacturer's defect warranty. ---
Black spots in the finish of enameled products are referred to as "carbon spots."
The carbon spots are the result of dust particles that get burned into the finish during the enamel firing process.
Carbons spots are a normal part of the manufacturing process. Typically, the spots are small and minimal, however the product should be inspected prior to installation. ---
Pot marks are caused by metal objects (most commonly aluminum cookware) striking the enameled surface and are not a manufacturing defect.
Pots, pans, and utensils may leave the metal marks on sink surfaces because the thick layer of fire-polished enameled is harder than cookware.
The pot marks look like scratches, but they do not penetrate the enameled surface.

To clean, apply a small amount of [KOHLER Cast Iron Cleaner (K-23725)](https://www.kohler.com/en/products/cleaners/shop-cleaners/cast-iron-cleaner-23725?skuId=23725-NA) to the marks. Use a soft cloth or cork to gently rub the marks away.
text:
Enameled Cast Iron Sink Care

# Restoring Luster to an Enameled Sink
- Enameled surfaces can lose the original luster with improper care and cleaning. Abrasive cleaners are not recommended.
- For detailed cleaning information and products to consider, visit [kohler.com/clean](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/how-to-use-kohler-cleaning-products).

---

# Discoloration from Rubber Mats
- Rubber dish mats are not recommended in KOHLER® sinks.
- Bacteria can grow under the mats and permanently discolor the enamel.
- Discoloration from rubber mats is not covered under the manufacturer's defect warranty.

---

# Black Spots In Enamel
- Black spots in the finish of enameled products are referred to as "carbon spots."
- The carbon spots are the result of dust particles that get burned into the finish during the enamel firing process.
- Carbons spots are a normal part of the manufacturing process. Typically, the spots are small and minimal, however the product should be inspected prior to installation.

---

# Removing Metal (Pot) Marks

- Pot marks are caused by metal objects (most commonly aluminum cookware) striking the enameled surface and are not a manufacturing defect.
- Pots, pans, and utensils may leave the metal marks on sink surfaces because the thick layer of fire-polished enameled is harder than cookware.
- The pot marks look like scratches, but they do not penetrate the enameled surface.
- To clean, apply a small amount of [KOHLER Cast Iron Cleaner (K-23725)](https://www.kohler.com/en/products/cleaners/shop-cleaners/cast-iron-cleaner-23725?skuId=23725-NA) to the marks. Use a soft cloth or cork to gently rub the marks away.

issue_description:

corrective_actions: The Gilford kitchen sink is designed for residential use.
This sink is only available with two faucet holes on 8" (203 mm) centers.
It is designed with a 3-5/8" (92 mm) diameter outlet to accommodate a standard kitchen sink drain and strainer. ---

Model K-12781 is a single center hole sink.

Camerton K-12867 and Tryell K-6676 are both blow-out service sinks.

The Harborview K-6607 sink does not ship with hangers or safety brackets. These items are included with the Harborview Legs K-6617.
If planning for a wall hung installation and custom legs, you will need to purchase four hangers and one safety bracket. ---
The inside of the K-6672 and K-6673 adjustable trap is enameled.
The outside is glazed ground coat to prevent rusting.

title: Sink Material Information
corrective_actions: Enamel is a powder coating applied to an iron casting and is a combination of clay, quartz, feldspar, silica, and color pigments.
When exposed to high temperatures, the coating melts and fuses to the casting, creating a glass-like surface.
The thickness of KOHLER® enamel provides outstanding protection against dents, chipping, and scratching while offering deep color integrity.
Enameled cast iron is available in a wide variety of colors and can be formed into unique shapes.
Enameled cast iron is made from recycled products and is recyclable. ---
Vitreous china is made from a clay base that is coated with a glaze and then fired at an intense heat to fuse the clay and glaze.
The ceramic materials of vitreous china offer a smooth, durable, nonporous surface that will not rust, fade, or discolor.
Vitreous china is ideal for intricate designs with a glossy finish. The material is often used in Artist Editions® sinks. ---
Fireclay sinks are made from dense clay that is heated and cured. The clay holds its shape through the firing process and maintains intricate designs and shapes.
The glazed sink surface is nonporous and easy to clean.
Fireclay is very durable and perfect for heavy-duty use. ---
Stainless steel is a durable, easy-to-clean material.
Typically made with a brushed finish, stainless steel can be polished to a mirror surface to highlight the design lines and product contours.

Products made from stainless steel may have different thicknesses, depending on the gauge of the steel. The lower the gauge, the thicker the material. Premium sinks are made from 16- and 18-gauge stainless steel.
text:
Sink Material Information

# Enameled Cast Iron
- Enamel is a powder coating applied to an iron casting and is a combination of clay, quartz, feldspar, silica, and color pigments.
- When exposed to high temperatures, the coating melts and fuses to the casting, creating a glass-like surface.
- The thickness of KOHLER® enamel provides outstanding protection against dents, chipping, and scratching while offering deep color integrity.
- Enameled cast iron is available in a wide variety of colors and can be formed into unique shapes.
- Enameled cast iron is made from recycled products and is recyclable.

---

# Vitreous China
- Vitreous china is made from a clay base that is coated with a glaze and then fired at an intense heat to fuse the clay and glaze.
- The ceramic materials of vitreous china offer a smooth, durable, nonporous surface that will not rust, fade, or discolor.
- Vitreous china is ideal for intricate designs with a glossy finish. The material is often used in Artist Editions® sinks.

---

# Fireclay
- Fireclay sinks are made from dense clay that is heated and cured. The clay holds its shape through the firing process and maintains intricate designs and shapes.
- The glazed sink surface is nonporous and easy to clean.
- Fireclay is very durable and perfect for heavy-duty use.

---

# Stainless Steel
- Stainless steel is a durable, easy-to-clean material.
- Typically made with a brushed finish, stainless steel can be polished to a mirror surface to highlight the design lines and product contours.
- Products made from stainless steel may have different thicknesses, depending on the gauge of the steel. The lower the gauge, the thicker the material. Premium sinks are made from 16- and 18-gauge stainless steel.

title: Adjusting Pop-Up Drains
issue_description:
- Review the written installation instructions that came with your drain. There is more than one type of drain and yours may vary slightly from the photos shown here.
- Pop-up drains work by attaching the lift rod on your faucet to a mechanism below called the linkage. The linkage connects to a part called the ball lever or ball rod assembly that is attached to the drain.

---
corrective_actions: If the drain stopper is not moving or closing, check the adjustable link.
Remove the clip that holds the link in place by squeezing the clip ends together.
Move the linkage up or down to a different hole to adjust the stopper movement.
Reinstall the clip.
Check stopper movement; readjust if necessary. ---
The ball rod holds the stopper in the drain. To reach the stopper, the ball rod needs to be removed first.
The ball rod is inserted into the side of the drain and attached with a nut.
To remove, unthread the rod nut, pull the ball rod out, and remove the stopper from the drain.
text:
Adjusting Pop-Up Drains

# Overview
- Review the written installation instructions that came with your drain. There is more than one type of drain and yours may vary slightly from the photos shown here.
- Pop-up drains work by attaching the lift rod on your faucet to a mechanism below called the linkage. The linkage connects to a part called the ball lever or ball rod assembly that is attached to the drain.

---

# Adjusting the Linkage

- If the drain stopper is not moving or closing, check the adjustable link.
- Remove the clip that holds the link in place by squeezing the clip ends together.
- Move the linkage up or down to a different hole to adjust the stopper movement.
- Reinstall the clip.
- Check stopper movement; readjust if necessary.

---

# Removing the Stopper
- The ball rod holds the stopper in the drain. To reach the stopper, the ball rod needs to be removed first.
- The ball rod is inserted into the side of the drain and attached with a nut.
- To remove, unthread the rod nut, pull the ball rod out, and remove the stopper from the drain.

title: Pedestal and Wall-Mount Bathroom Sinks Installation Information

title: Install Shower Door Rollers
issue_description:
Although Kohler and Sterling use several different types of rollers for their shower doors, the basic installation and replacement of all the rollers are the same. Proper installation is important as incorrect installation can cause the doors to slide poorly, make grinding noises, and/or even jump the track.  However, ensuring that the rollers are correctly installed is quite simple to do.

When installing the rollers, the "nut side" of the roller will always be installed against the top frame flange or hanging bracket of the door. 

The outside of the roller will always face the same way as the panel you are attaching it to. If you are installing rollers on the outside panel (the panel closest to you when standing outside the bath/ shower enclosure) the outside face of the rollers will be facing you when you are standing outside the unit.

Outside Panel: Outside face of roller faces out into the room

Inside Panel: Outside face of the roller faces into the shower/bath  

If the rollers are installed correctly and the panels still do not slide easily, check to make sure there is no debris in the roller channels inside the top track of the shower door.

title: Unlevel or Imperfect Bottom Shower Door Track
issue_description:
It is very critical that the bottom track for a shower door or bath door installation is set on a level surface. Additionally, there must be no imperfections in the bottom track. While Kohler and Sterling inspects each batch of tracks for defects, we recommend you inspect the product prior to installation to ensure there are no other imperfections.

If the bottom track does not sit level, the door will not install, open or close properly. More importantly, any water caught on the track will not gravitate back onto the receptor or drain.
