title: Levity® Shower Doors - Roller Installation and Adjustment
issue_description:
The rollers for the Levity sliding shower door are designed to allow easy out-of-plumb adjustment. The following sections describe proper roller assembly and adjustment.

WARNING: The rollers for the outside door include anti-jump clips. Proper installation of the clips is critical for door safety.

NOTE: The rollers for the inside door contain a brass bushing.

NOTE: The holes for the inside rollers and outside rollers are in different locations on the door panels.

---

After the door panels are installed, the rollers can be adjusted for out-of-plumb conditions. Alignment is achieved by rotating the cam.
corrective_actions: The inside glass door panel is positioned closest to the shower. The holes for the rollers are 4-3/8" (111 mm) from the top of the glass. The inside door roller components are assembled to the glass panel as shown. Install each inside roller with the tab on top. This will position the door at its highest setting, allowing for easier adjustment if necessary. The screw is secured into the brass insert. ---

The outside glass door panel is positioned closest to the shower. The holes for the rollers are 2-1/4" (57 mm) from the top of the glass. The outside roller components are assembled to the glass panel and secured with a screw as shown. Install the outside rollers with the tab on the clamp on top. Hold the clip downward as the screw is tightened. WARNING: The rollers for the outside door include anti-jump clips. Proper installation of the clips is critical for door safety. The hooks of the clips should be positioned inside the header ---

Remove the cap to access the cam. Loosen the screw. Rotate both cams to adjust door height uniformly.  Rotate one cam to rotate the door to correct an out-of-plumb condition. NOTE: The door will be at its highest position when the raised portion of the cam is located at the top. IMPORTANT! Make sure the screw is retightened before reinstalling the cap. Once door alignment is achieved, tighten the screw. Reinstall the cap.
text:
Levity® Shower Doors - Roller Installation and Adjustment

# Overview
The rollers for the Levity sliding shower door are designed to allow easy out-of-plumb adjustment. The following sections describe proper roller assembly and adjustment.

WARNING: The rollers for the outside door include anti-jump clips. Proper installation of the clips is critical for door safety.

NOTE: The rollers for the inside door contain a brass bushing.

NOTE: The holes for the inside rollers and outside rollers are in different locations on the door panels.

---

# Roller Assembly - Inside Door

 The inside glass door panel is positioned closest to the shower.
 The holes for the rollers are 4-3/8" (111 mm) from the top of the glass.

 The inside door roller components are assembled to the glass panel as shown.
 Install each inside roller with the tab on top. This will position the door at its highest setting, allowing for easier adjustment if necessary.
 The screw is secured into the brass insert.

---

# Roller Assembly - Outside Door

 The outside glass door panel is positioned closest to the shower.
 The holes for the rollers are 2-1/4" (57 mm) from the top of the glass.

 The outside roller components are assembled to the glass panel and secured with a screw as shown.
 Install the outside rollers with the tab on the clamp on top.
 Hold the clip downward as the screw is tightened. 

WARNING: The rollers for the outside door include anti-jump clips. Proper installation of the clips is critical for door safety.

 The hooks of the clips should be positioned inside the header

---

# Door Alignment

After the door panels are installed, the rollers can be adjusted for out-of-plumb conditions. Alignment is achieved by rotating the cam.

# Roller Adjustment
 Remove the cap to access the cam.
Loosen the screw.
 Rotate both cams to adjust door height uniformly.  Rotate one cam to rotate the door to correct an out-of-plumb condition.
NOTE: The door will be at its highest position when the raised portion of the cam is located at the top.

IMPORTANT! Make sure the screw is retightened before reinstalling the cap.

 Once door alignment is achieved, tighten the screw.
 Reinstall the cap.

title: Levity® Bath/Shower Door - Centerguide Replacement
corrective_actions: Lift the threshold seal to access the screw. Loosen the screw with a 5/32" hex wrench. Slide the centerguide down the threshold until it clears the door panels. Lift the centerguide from the threshold lip. ---

IMPORTANT! The centerguide must be fully seated behind the threshold lip as shown. Slide both door panels to one end of the shower. Thread the screw partially into the centerguide hole.  Ensure the end of the screw does not protrude from the bottom of the centerguide. Measure and mark the centerline of the threshold on the outside of the shower base/bath ledge. Rotate the centerguide into place in the threshold groove as shown. Slide the centerguide down the threshold until the screw aligns with the centerline mark. Slide the door panels into the centerguide channels. Lift the threshold seal to access the screw. Handtighten the screw with a 5/32″ hex wrench, then tighten an additional one half turn.
text:
Levity® Bath/Shower Door - Centerguide Replacement

# Remove the Existing Centerguide

 Lift the threshold seal to access the screw.
 Loosen the screw with a 5/32" hex wrench.
 Slide the centerguide down the threshold until it clears the door panels.
 Lift the centerguide from the threshold lip.

---

# Install the New Centerguide

IMPORTANT! The centerguide must be fully seated behind the threshold lip as shown.

 Slide both door panels to one end of the shower.
Thread the screw partially into the centerguide hole.  Ensure the end of the screw does not protrude from the bottom of the centerguide.

 Measure and mark the centerline of the threshold on the outside of the shower base/bath ledge.
 Rotate the centerguide into place in the threshold groove as shown.
 Slide the centerguide down the threshold until the screw aligns with the centerline mark.
 Slide the door panels into the centerguide channels.
 Lift the threshold seal to access the screw.
 Handtighten the screw with a 5/32″ hex wrench, then tighten an additional one half turn.

title: Shower Door Wall Anchors Installation
issue_description:
There are two main types of wall anchors in hardware packs for KOHLER® and STERLING® shower doors: standard drywall anchors and hollow wall anchors.
 Hardware packs for any shower door model will contain one or the other style of anchor, but will not contain both.
 If different style anchors are needed for your application, they can be purchased at any hardware store.

Mark and drill a hole at the intended anchor location on the wall. For tile, use a masonry bit.
 Insert the anchor into the hole.
 Use a hammer to install the anchor flush with the wall.

Mark and drill a hole at the intended anchor location on the wall. For tile, use a masonry bit.
 Fold the ends of anchor together and insert into the hole.
NOTE: For detailed installation instructions, refer to the installation guide provided with your product.
corrective_actions: NOTE: If there is a stud located in the wall where the wall jamb will be installed, you do not need to use anchors. Screws or fasteners can be attached directly to the stud and will sufficiently support the wall jamb.
text:
Shower Door Wall Anchors Installation

# Overview

 There are two main types of wall anchors in hardware packs for KOHLER® and STERLING® shower doors: standard drywall anchors and hollow wall anchors.
 Hardware packs for any shower door model will contain one or the other style of anchor, but will not contain both.
 If different style anchors are needed for your application, they can be purchased at any hardware store.

# Anchor Installation

NOTE: If there is a stud located in the wall where the wall jamb will be installed, you do not need to use anchors. Screws or fasteners can be attached directly to the stud and will sufficiently support the wall jamb.

# Standard Wall Anchors

 Mark and drill a hole at the intended anchor location on the wall. For tile, use a masonry bit.
 Insert the anchor into the hole.
 Use a hammer to install the anchor flush with the wall.

# Hollow Wall Anchors

 Mark and drill a hole at the intended anchor location on the wall. For tile, use a masonry bit.
 Fold the ends of anchor together and insert into the hole.
NOTE: For detailed installation instructions, refer to the installation guide provided with your product.

title: Hole Drilling Location for a 1500D Series Shower Door
issue_description:
The installation and design of the Sterling 1500D Series shower door has been changed to provide an easier installation experience. The parts kit now includes a drilling template. The drilling template is intended to assist the installer in locating and installing the bottom pivot hole.

If the drilling template happens to be missing from the parts package, you can use the dimensions indicated below to drill the 5/16" hole into the bottom track.

After you determine which side should open, and the fixed panel is installed, then you may use the template to drill the hole. 

The bottom pivot hole should be drilled at .500 inches away from the u-channel, and the center of the hole should be centered on the bottom track which is .315 inches from the edge of the track. See the attached image of the Drilling Template for further detail.

text:
Steam Generator Power Clean™ Function

# When to Use the Power Clean Function
 Users will be automatically reminded to use Power Clean after 600 minutes of steam generator use. The steam control panel will display "run," "PCLn."
 The steam generator may be run three times before the cleaning function must be activated.
 The cleaning cycle must be complete before normal steam operation can be resumed.

---

# Activating Power Clean

WARNING: Risk of personal injury. Stay out of the showering area when the Power Clean function is operating.

Note: When Power Clean is activated, water will typically discharge from the steam head.

Note: If electrical power to the steam generator is interrupted during the cleaning cycle, the cycle must be restarted when the electrical power is restored.

 Press and hold the timer, increase, and decrease buttons at the same time for 5 seconds.
 The display will read "PCLn," "On," then will count down the cycle time until the cleaning cycle is complete.
 The cleaning cycle may last up to 45 minutes, then shuts off automatically when complete.

title: Remove the Plug on the K-728 Transfer Valve
issue_description:
The K-728 Transfer Valve includes an internal plug that creates three ports inside the valve. Removal of that plug will change the valve from a three-way valve to a two-way valve. The NPT plug that is in the center of the brass body of the transfer valve separates outlets B and C for three-way installations. When this plug is removed, it creates the connection between the two allowing either or both to be used for the secondary function.

Kohler recommends to use a large head screwdriver that fills the slot in the plastic internal plug to remove it from the valve body; you must also push firmly to push the plug out.
text:
Remove the Plug on the K-728 Transfer Valve

The K-728 Transfer Valve includes an internal plug that creates three ports inside the valve. Removal of that plug will change the valve from a three-way valve to a two-way valve. The NPT plug that is in the center of the brass body of the transfer valve separates outlets B and C for three-way installations. When this plug is removed, it creates the connection between the two allowing either or both to be used for the secondary function.

Kohler recommends to use a large head screwdriver that fills the slot in the plastic internal plug to remove it from the valve body; you must also push firmly to push the plug out.

title: Remove the Handles for the MasterShower Valve Trim
issue_description: The following directions describe removal of the Mastershower Rite-Temp, Thermostatic, Volume, and Transfer Valve Trims.
corrective_actions: Gently pry off the cap in the center of the handle using a thin flat blade such as a screwdriver, taking care to protect all finish surfaces.
Unscrew the Philips screw attaching the handle to the stem.

Remove the two screws holding the escutcheon plate with a Philips screwdriver.
Set all parts aside for re-use.

text:

title: Pressure-Balancing Unit (PBU)
corrective_actions: Discard the thick washers (#1 from Fig. 1). These washers are only used when installing a PBU in the Coralais® K-15877 valve. If installing a new PBU with an existing mixer cap, install the medium O-rings, (#2 from Fig. 1), and large O-ring, (#4 from Fig. 1), onto the existing mixer cap (Fig. 2). NOTE: If installing a new PBU with a new mixer cap, the new mixer cap will include the new medium O-rings and large O-ring. NOTE: If installing a new PBU with an early pressure-balancing valve brass cap (three-ribbed stem model), the installation requires the GP876851 mixer and PBU combination. See the "Identify a Single Control Bath/Shower Valve" help topic for more information. Place the small O-rings, (#3 from Fig 1), on the back of the PBU. The PBU location for the O-rings is oval-shaped but the small O-rings are flexible enough to fit into the location (Fig. 3). Proceed by reinstalling the PBU and mixer cap into the valve body. ---

Discard the medium O-rings, (#2 from Fig. 1), as the Coralais K-15877 mixer cap does not use these O-rings. Place the small O-rings, (#3 from Fig. 1), on the back of the PBU. The PBU location for the O-rings is oval shaped but the small O-rings are flexible enough to fit into the location (Fig. 4). Place the thick washers, (#1 from Fig. 1), on the front of the PBU (Fig. 4). Install the large O-ring on the back of the grey PBU adapter plate (Fig. 5). Reassemble the remainder of the valve (Fig. 6).
text:
Pressure-Balancing Unit (PBU)

# K-304 or K-15701 PBU Installation

 Discard the thick washers (#1 from Fig. 1). These washers are only used when installing a PBU in the Coralais® K-15877 valve.
 If installing a new PBU with an existing mixer cap, install the medium O-rings, (#2 from Fig. 1), and large O-ring, (#4 from Fig. 1), onto the existing mixer cap (Fig. 2).

NOTE: If installing a new PBU with a new mixer cap, the new mixer cap will include the new medium O-rings and large O-ring.

NOTE: If installing a new PBU with an early pressure-balancing valve brass cap (three-ribbed stem model), the installation requires the GP876851 mixer and PBU combination. See the "Identify a Single Control Bath/Shower Valve" help topic for more information.

 Place the small O-rings, (#3 from Fig 1), on the back of the PBU. The PBU location for the O-rings is oval-shaped but the small O-rings are flexible enough to fit into the location (Fig. 3).
 Proceed by reinstalling the PBU and mixer cap into the valve body.

---

# Coralais® K-15877 PBU Installation

 Discard the medium O-rings, (#2 from Fig. 1), as the Coralais K-15877 mixer cap does not use these O-rings.
 Place the small O-rings, (#3 from Fig. 1), on the back of the PBU. The PBU location for the O-rings is oval shaped but the small O-rings are flexible enough to fit into the location (Fig. 4).
 Place the thick washers, (#1 from Fig. 1), on the front of the PBU (Fig. 4).
 Install the large O-ring on the back of the grey PBU adapter plate (Fig. 5).
 Reassemble the remainder of the valve (Fig. 6).

title: K-304 Valve - Adding a Transfer/Diverter Valve
issue_description:
K-304- Rite-Temp® Pressure Balancing Valve

---

If additional ports are needed for your shower configuration when using a K-304 valve, an additional valve can be added above the top port at the location shown.
 Kohler Co. recommends a K-728 transfer valve or K-737 diverter valve be installed following the installation instructions provided with the valve.
 For more information on the K-728 transfer valve or K-737 diverter valve, including installation instructions, go to the product page at [www.us.kohler.com.](http://www.us.kohler.com/)

---

IMPORTANT: Do not install a valve with a shut-off after the shower port, as this may result in cross-flow between ports.

Note: If the transfer or diverter valve is only being used as a 2-way valve, a 2-way conversion must be completed following the instructions provided with the valve.

Note: The standard installation orientation of the K-304 valve has the shower port facing up.

Note: The shower outlet only allows 4 gpm (15 lpm) flow rate. If a shower and handshower will be used at the same time, there may be low flow unless lower flow devices are installed.

 Install the K-304 following the instructions provided with the valve.
 Install a K-728 transfer valve or K-737 diverter valve in-line with the top outlet following the instructions provided with the valve.
 If two outlets will be used, convert the K-728 or K-737 valve to a 2-way valve following the instructions provided with the valve.

Note: The K-304 valve will act as volume and temperature control.

Note: Depending on the settings on the diverter valve, the bath may not be the first component to turn on.

Note: The bath outlet allows 5 gpm (19 lpm) flow rate. Flow rate should be adequate for a typical shower and handshower being used at the same time.

 Install the K-304 following the instructions provided with the valve, but rotate the valve 180 degrees so the bath spout outlet is on top.
 Cap the valve outlet port on the bottom of the K-304 after it is rotated.
 Install a K-728 transfer valve or K-737 diverter valve in-line with the top outlet following the instructions provided with the valve.
 Plumb the components to the 3-way diverter.
text:
K-304 Valve - Adding a Transfer/Diverter Valve

# Affected SKUs
K-304- Rite-Temp® Pressure Balancing Valve

---

# If K-304 Needs Additional Outlets

 If additional ports are needed for your shower configuration when using a K-304 valve, an additional valve can be added above the top port at the location shown.
 Kohler Co. recommends a K-728 transfer valve or K-737 diverter valve be installed following the installation instructions provided with the valve.
 For more information on the K-728 transfer valve or K-737 diverter valve, including installation instructions, go to the product page at [www.us.kohler.com.](http://www.us.kohler.com/)

---

# Configuration Options

IMPORTANT: Do not install a valve with a shut-off after the shower port, as this may result in cross-flow between ports.

Note: If the transfer or diverter valve is only being used as a 2-way valve, a 2-way conversion must be completed following the instructions provided with the valve.

# Option 1 - Shower Port Facing Up

Note: The standard installation orientation of the K-304 valve has the shower port facing up.

Note: The shower outlet only allows 4 gpm (15 lpm) flow rate. If a shower and handshower will be used at the same time, there may be low flow unless lower flow devices are installed.

 Install the K-304 following the instructions provided with the valve.
 Install a K-728 transfer valve or K-737 diverter valve in-line with the top outlet following the instructions provided with the valve.
 If two outlets will be used, convert the K-728 or K-737 valve to a 2-way valve following the instructions provided with the valve.

# Option 2 - Bath Spout Port Facing Up
Note: The K-304 valve will act as volume and temperature control.

Note: Depending on the settings on the diverter valve, the bath may not be the first component to turn on.

Note: The bath outlet allows 5 gpm (19 lpm) flow rate. Flow rate should be adequate for a typical shower and handshower being used at the same time.

 Install the K-304 following the instructions provided with the valve, but rotate the valve 180 degrees so the bath spout outlet is on top.
 Cap the valve outlet port on the bottom of the K-304 after it is rotated.
 Install a K-728 transfer valve or K-737 diverter valve in-line with the top outlet following the instructions provided with the valve.
 Plumb the components to the 3-way diverter.

title: Bath Spouts
issue_description:
A slip-fit spout has an internal assembly that slips over a copper pipe.
 The spout has an opening on the bottom side where a setscrew is tightened to hold the spout onto the copper pipe.
 A slip-fit spout does not contain threads.

NPT refers to a standard thread size in the plumbing industry.
 An NPT spout has internal threads for threading onto a pipe nipple.
 The spout has an opening on the bottom side, but there is no setscrew. The pipe nipple would be visible inside the opening.
text:
Bath Spouts

# Slip-Fit Versus Threaded

# Slip-Fit Spout:
 A slip-fit spout has an internal assembly that slips over a copper pipe.
 The spout has an opening on the bottom side where a setscrew is tightened to hold the spout onto the copper pipe.
 A slip-fit spout does not contain threads.

# Threaded NPT Spout:
 NPT refers to a standard thread size in the plumbing industry.
 An NPT spout has internal threads for threading onto a pipe nipple.
 The spout has an opening on the bottom side, but there is no setscrew. The pipe nipple would be visible inside the opening.

title: Stillness® and Purist® Bath Fillers - Temperature Adjustment
issue_description:
The Stillness and Purist floor-mount bath fillers have an adjustable limit stop used to set maximum water temperature.

Stillness K-994-4 (discontinued) and K-T97344–.
 Purist K-10129-4 (discontinued) and K-T97328–.

---

Using a hex wrench, loosen the three internal setscrews in the top of the brass stop. Remove the stop.
 Remove the red plastic limit stop and reposition it to the desired location.
 Turn the valve on and test the water temperature with a thermometer.
 Continue to reposition the red limit stop until the desired maximum water temperature is achieved.
 Reinstall the brass stop, making sure that the external screwhead is in the same location as before the stop was removed.
corrective_actions: Using a flat-blade screwdriver, remove the plug button in the handle. Using a hex wrench, loosen the setscrew in the bottom of the handle and remove the handle. IMPORTANT: Note the location of the external screwhead in the brass stop before you remove the stop. When the stop is reinstalled, the external screwhead must be in the same location.

Place the handle onto the valve and verify that the nut does not show. If the nut is visible, tighten the nut further. Be sure to push the handle straight down onto the valve. When the nut is no longer visible, tighten the three setscrews in the stop. Reinstall the handle by tightening the setscrew in the bottom of the handle. Replace the plug button.
text:
Stillness® and Purist® Bath Fillers - Temperature Adjustment

# Overview
 The Stillness and Purist floor-mount bath fillers have an adjustable limit stop used to set maximum water temperature.

# Affected SKUs:
 Stillness K-994-4 (discontinued) and K-T97344–.
 Purist K-10129-4 (discontinued) and K-T97328–.

---

# Adjust the Maximum Water Temperature

# Remove the Handle
 Using a flat-blade screwdriver, remove the plug button in the handle.
 Using a hex wrench, loosen the setscrew in the bottom of the handle and remove the handle.

IMPORTANT: Note the location of the external screwhead in the brass stop before you remove the stop. When the stop is reinstalled, the external screwhead must be in the same location.

# Reposition the Stop
 Using a hex wrench, loosen the three internal setscrews in the top of the brass stop. Remove the stop.
 Remove the red plastic limit stop and reposition it to the desired location.
 Turn the valve on and test the water temperature with a thermometer.
 Continue to reposition the red limit stop until the desired maximum water temperature is achieved.
 Reinstall the brass stop, making sure that the external screwhead is in the same location as before the stop was removed.

# Reinstall the Handle
 Place the handle onto the valve and verify that the nut does not show. If the nut is visible, tighten the nut further.
 Be sure to push the handle straight down onto the valve.
 When the nut is no longer visible, tighten the three setscrews in the stop.
 Reinstall the handle by tightening the setscrew in the bottom of the handle.
 Replace the plug button.

title: How to Swap the Anthem Supply Stops to Reverse Hot and Cold Water Supply Lines
issue_description:
Note: Proper installation of the Anthem Mechanical Valve requires the hot water supply line comes into the top inlet port and the cold water supply line comes into the bottom inlet port. The proper orientation of the valve is indicated by a red QC sticker. 

The Stops are pre-installed into the valve and are marked with H or C on Stop face.
corrective_actions: 4mm Hex Wrench 8mm Hex Wrench Needle Nose Pliers
Turn the water off to the entire building or at the shut off Valve.
Remove Thermostatic Trim.
Use a 4mm hex wrench to partially unthread the screws that hold the Retention Nuts.

Insert the 8mm hex wrench into the center of the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly and turn the assembly counterclockwise until the assembly begins to push up on the Retention Nut. As needed, unthread the Retention Nut screws a little at a time and continue to turn counterclockwise. Doing so makes it easier to remove the Retention Nut from the Supply Stop Body assembly in Step 7 Note: During the unthreading process, the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly must turn together. If the Stop Body and Check Valve do not turn together, turn the assembly clockwise until it is tight in the Stop Body and then continue to rotate together counterclockwise.
Fully remove the three Retention Nut screws.
Use needle nose pliers to grip the Retention Nut and pull out the Stop Body Assembly. Be careful not to grip and damage any threads.
Unthread the Retention Nut from Stop Body. (Retention Nut is reverse threaded)
Repeat Steps 1-7 to remove the other Stop Body assembly.

Reinsert the Stop Body assembly into the opposite cavity: Starting with the top Stop Body, push it fully into the cavity until it clicks into place. Place the Retention Nut on the Stop Body. NOTE: The Retention Nuts cannot be swapped into the top or bottom cavity; they must remain in their original orientation. Use the 8 mm hex wrench to turn the Stop Body clockwise until it stops rotating. TIP: Hold the Retention Nut while rotating the Stop Body to keep it in place. Back off the rotation as needed to align the Retention Nut screw with the screw hole. Partially thread the top Retention Nut screw using the 4 mm hex wrench. The Stop is open when the thread of the Stop Body protrudes from the Retention Nut.
Repeat Step 9 to reinsert the bottom Stop Body. Then reinstall the rest of the Retention Nut screws.
Evenly tighten the three Retention Nut screws to ensure they are flush with the Retention Nut.

Re-install the temperature handle assembly and trim faceplate and turn on an outlet to test the water flow. Use temperature knob to confirm proper hot and cold operation. --- Kohler Service Part Numbers: 1411262 Hot Service Stop Assembly 1411258 Cold Service Stop Assembly
text:
How to Swap the Anthem Supply Stops to Reverse Hot and Cold Water Supply Lines

Note: Proper installation of the Anthem Mechanical Valve requires the hot water supply line comes into the top inlet port and the cold water supply line comes into the bottom inlet port. The proper orientation of the valve is indicated by a red QC sticker. 

The Stops are pre-installed into the valve and are marked with H or C on Stop face.

# Tools Needed:
 4mm Hex Wrench
 8mm Hex Wrench
 Needle Nose Pliers

1.
Turn the water off to the entire building or at the shut off Valve.

2.
Remove Thermostatic Trim.

3.
Use a 4mm hex wrench to partially unthread the screws that hold the Retention Nuts.

4.
Insert the 8mm hex wrench into the center of the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly and turn the assembly counterclockwise until the assembly begins to push up on the Retention Nut. As needed, unthread the Retention Nut screws a little at a time and continue to turn counterclockwise. Doing so makes it easier to remove the Retention Nut from the Supply Stop Body assembly in Step 7

Note: During the unthreading process, the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly must turn together. If the Stop Body and Check Valve do not turn together, turn the assembly clockwise until it is tight in the Stop Body and then continue to rotate together counterclockwise.

5.
Fully remove the three Retention Nut screws.

6.
Use needle nose pliers to grip the Retention Nut and pull out the Stop Body Assembly. Be careful not to grip and damage any threads.

7.
Unthread the Retention Nut from Stop Body. (Retention Nut is reverse threaded)

8.
Repeat Steps 1-7 to remove the other Stop Body assembly.

9.
Reinsert the Stop Body assembly into the opposite cavity:

 Starting with the top Stop Body, push it fully into the cavity until it clicks into place.
 Place the Retention Nut on the Stop Body. NOTE: The Retention Nuts cannot be swapped into the top or bottom cavity; they must remain in their original orientation.
 Use the 8 mm hex wrench to turn the Stop Body clockwise until it stops rotating.
TIP: Hold the Retention Nut while rotating the Stop Body to keep it in place. Back off the rotation as needed to align the Retention Nut screw with the screw hole.
 Partially thread the top Retention Nut screw using the 4 mm hex wrench.
 The Stop is open when the thread of the Stop Body protrudes from the Retention Nut. 

10.
Repeat Step 9 to reinsert the bottom Stop Body. Then reinstall the rest of the Retention Nut screws.

11.
Evenly tighten the three Retention Nut screws to ensure they are flush with the Retention Nut.

12.
Re-install the temperature handle assembly and trim faceplate and turn on an outlet to test the water flow. Use temperature knob to confirm proper hot and cold operation.

---

title: Bath Spout Slip-fit Assembly
issue_description:
Slip-fit bath spouts contain a slip-fit assembly that is held in place with a setscrew.
 For threaded installations, the slip-fit assembly is removed by loosening the setscrew so the spout can be threaded onto the pipe.
 For slip-fit installations, the setscrew should not be loosened because the slip-fit assembly must stay in place.
 If the slip-fit assembly was mistakenly removed, it can be reinstalled into the spout, but this may be difficult.
 The recommended procedure for slip-fit reinstallation is shown below.

---
corrective_actions: The slip-fit assembly consists of a two-piece clamp, two washers, and an O-ring. The clamp pieces fit together, but are not fastened to each other. The challenge is holding the two pieces together while inserting them into the bath spout. To hold the clamp pieces, firmly grip the two halves together with a needle nose pliers. Slip the assembly back into the grooves inside the spout. Secure the assembly in place by tightening the setscrew.

 The recommended procedure for slip-fit reinstallation is shown below.

---

# Slip-fit Assembly Installation

 The slip-fit assembly consists of a two-piece clamp, two washers, and an O-ring.
 The clamp pieces fit together, but are not fastened to each other. The challenge is holding the two pieces together while inserting them into the bath spout.
 To hold the clamp pieces, firmly grip the two halves together with a needle nose pliers.
 Slip the assembly back into the grooves inside the spout.
 Secure the assembly in place by tightening the setscrew.

title: Adjust the Temperature on a Rite-Temp Shower Valve
issue_description:
The K-304- Rite-Temp Valves may be adjusted to achieve your maximum hot water temperature. Note: The water temperature should never be set above 120 degrees F.

1.
Remove the handle and trim from the wall to expose the cap assembly.

2.
Remove the black o-ring, caution tag, and red collar from the round brass stem; older model will have a black collar.

3.
Rotate the valve stem clockwise to turn the water on. Test the water temperature with a thermometer.

4.
When the desired water temperature has been reached, replace the red or black collar on the valve stem.

5.
Turn the stem counterclockwise to turn the water off.

6.
Reinstall the caution tag, o-ring, trim, and handle.

title: Handshower Backflow Prevention Devices
issue_description:
Plumbing codes require that hand-held showers be provided with backflow protection.
 Backflow protection can be an air gap, two independent check valves, or a vacuum breaker.
 All KOHLER® handshowers contain an integral check valve, which also functions as a flow control.
 If a second check valve is required, a handshower hose that contains a check valve should be used.
 If additional backflow prevention is required, installation of the K-9660 vacuum breaker is recommended.
 Refer to the product specification sheet for the presence of check valves for backflow protection.

title: How to Open or Close the Anthem Supply Stops
issue_description: 8mm Hex Wrench
corrective_actions: Remove the temperature handle assembly and trim faceplate with the Kohler logo.

Insert the 8mm hex wrench into the center of the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly and turn the assembly clockwise until it stops rotating. Note: During the clockwise rotation, the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly must turn together. If the Stop Body and Check Valve do not turn together, turn the hex wrench clockwise until the Check Valve is tight in the Stop Body. Note: Do not remove the Check Valve from the Stop Body as doing so will cause water to come out of the valve because they do not stop the water from flowing.
The Supply Stop is open when the thread of the Supply Stop protrudes above the Retention Nut and can no longer rotate clockwise.  Water will flow to the outlets. Example of Open Supply Stop
Repeat Steps 1 & 2 for the other Stop Body.
Turn the water off at the shut off valve.
Remove the temperature handle assembly and trim faceplate with the Kohler logo.

Insert the 8mm hex wrench into the center of the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly and turn the assembly counterclockwise until it stops rotating. Note: During the counterclockwise rotation, the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly must turn together. If the Stop Body and Check Valve do not turn together, turn the hex wrench clockwise until the Check Valve is tight in the Stop Body. Note: Do not remove the Check Valve from the Stop Body as doing so will cause water to come out of the valve because they do not stop the water from flowing.

The Supply Stop is closed when the Supply Stop thread is recessed below the top of the Retention Nut and can no longer rotate counterclockwise. Water will not flow to the outlets. Example of Open Supply Stop
Repeat Steps 2 & 3 for the other Supply Stop Body.
text:
How to Open or Close the Anthem Supply Stops

# Tools Needed: 
 8mm Hex Wrench

# To Open the Water Supply Stops
1.
Remove the temperature handle assembly and trim faceplate with the Kohler logo.

2.
Insert the 8mm hex wrench into the center of the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly and turn the assembly clockwise until it stops rotating.

Note: During the clockwise rotation, the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly must turn together. If the Stop Body and Check Valve do not turn together, turn the hex wrench clockwise until the Check Valve is tight in the Stop Body.

Note: Do not remove the Check Valve from the Stop Body as doing so will cause water to come out of the valve because they do not stop the water from flowing.

3.
The Supply Stop is open when the thread of the Supply Stop protrudes above the Retention Nut and can no longer rotate clockwise.  Water will flow to the outlets.

Example of Open Supply Stop
 
4.
Repeat Steps 1 & 2 for the other Stop Body.

# To Close the Water Supply Stops

1.
Turn the water off at the shut off valve.

2.
Remove the temperature handle assembly and trim faceplate with the Kohler logo.

3.
Insert the 8mm hex wrench into the center of the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly and turn the assembly counterclockwise until it stops rotating. 

Note: During the counterclockwise rotation, the Stop Body/Check Valve assembly must turn together. If the Stop Body and Check Valve do not turn together, turn the hex wrench clockwise until the Check Valve is tight in the Stop Body.

Note: Do not remove the Check Valve from the Stop Body as doing so will cause water to come out of the valve because they do not stop the water from flowing.

4.
The Supply Stop is closed when the Supply Stop thread is recessed below the top of the Retention Nut and can no longer rotate counterclockwise. Water will not flow to the outlets.

Example of Open Supply Stop

5. Repeat Steps 2 & 3 for the other Supply Stop Body.

title: Remove Minor Scratching from Lithocast Material
issue_description:
Your solid surface acrylic bath is strong and durable, and will provide you with years of satisfaction. If you observe stains or minor scratches in the acrylic surface, follow these steps to quickly repair your bath.
 
IMPORTANT! This repair procedure is not appropriate for deep scratches, gouges, or chips. For damage of that nature please contact Kohler Co. or a local solid surface repair professional.

NOTE: We recommend wet sanding to extend the life of the sandpaper, although dry sanding will produce the same quality repair.

NOTE: Use 400 grit sandpaper to remove scratches and stains.
corrective_actions: Apply flat, even pressure with the sandpaper and move the paper in a circular pattern.
Inspect your progress frequently to ensure a quality repair.
Clean or replace the sandpaper as needed during the repair.
When the damage is repaired, polish the area with clean 600 grit sandpaper.
Use a steady circular motion to polish the repaired surface and surrounding area to restore the bath to its original finish.
When you are finished, rinse the bath surface with clean water to remove any sanding dust and debris.
Use a clean cloth to dry the bath surface. This information can be found in the [Homeowners Guide](http://www.us.kohler.com/onlinecatalog/pdf/11451305.pdf) of any Lithocast product.

title: Lithocast™ Bath - Toe-Tap Drain Change
corrective_actions: An engineering change was made to the toe-tap drain clicker assembly on Lithocast baths.
Affected products are K-1800, K-1801, and K-1805.
The new assembly contains a V-groove that provides a more effective surface for the clicker setscrew to stay in place.
The change provides a better long-term drain seal. ---
NOTE: Detach the cover and insert from the clicker assembly if reusing these parts on the new assembly. Remove the Old Assembly
Carefully pull up on the cover to lift the clicker assembly from the drain body.
If needed, use a hex wrench to remove the setscrews holding the cover to the clicker assembly.
If needed, use a hex wrench to remove the setscrew securing the insert to the assembly.
Retain all setscrews.
Discard the old clicker assembly. Install the New Assembly
Place the cover and insert onto the new clicker assembly.
Make sure the concave side of the gasket is facing down. The drain may not seal properly if the gasket is flipped.
Add a drop of removable thread locking sealant (such as Loctite® 242) to all retained setscrews.
Reinstall and tighten the setscrews to secure the cover and the insert to the new clicker assembly.
Align the tabs on the insert with the slots in the drain body.
Press the assembly fully down into the drain body.
Close the drain and fill the bath with water to confirm proper drain operation.
text:
Lithocast™ Bath - Toe-Tap Drain Change

# Clicker Assembly Part Change

- An engineering change was made to the toe-tap drain clicker assembly on Lithocast baths.
- Affected products are K-1800, K-1801, and K-1805.
- The new assembly contains a V-groove that provides a more effective surface for the clicker setscrew to stay in place.
- The change provides a better long-term drain seal.

---

# Clicker Assembly Replacement

NOTE: Detach the cover and insert from the clicker assembly if reusing these parts on the new assembly.

Remove the Old Assembly

- Carefully pull up on the cover to lift the clicker assembly from the drain body.
- If needed, use a hex wrench to remove the setscrews holding the cover to the clicker assembly.
- If needed, use a hex wrench to remove the setscrew securing the insert to the assembly.
- Retain all setscrews.
- Discard the old clicker assembly.

Install the New Assembly

- Place the cover and insert onto the new clicker assembly.
- Make sure the concave side of the gasket is facing down. The drain may not seal properly if the gasket is flipped.
- Add a drop of removable thread locking sealant (such as Loctite® 242) to all retained setscrews.
- Reinstall and tighten the setscrews to secure the cover and the insert to the new clicker assembly.
- Align the tabs on the insert with the slots in the drain body.
- Press the assembly fully down into the drain body.
- Close the drain and fill the bath with water to confirm proper drain operation.

title: K-1446 Remote Blower Kit Installation
issue_description:
- KOHLER BubbleMassage™ air baths come equipped with a coiled section of 1" flexible PVC piping between the bath and the blower motor.
- The coiled piping must remain intact to prevent back flow of water into the blower assembly.
- When relocating the blower, it is important to avoid cutting, removing, or uncoiling any part of the coiled piping.

---
corrective_actions: IMPORTANT: Do not cut, remove, or uncoil any part of the coiled piping.
Cut the middle of the 1-1/2" PVC pipe located between the tee and the union nut.
Disconnect and remove the cable between the blower and the user interface.
Cut the straps holding the blower motor to the support board on the bath. ---

Note: Locate the blower motor within 15' (4.6 m) of the bath, with no more than six direction changes in the piping. Note: The blower motor must be oriented horizontally, and installed to a support block no lower than the original mounted height relative to the bath.
At the new location, mount the blower on a minimum 1-1/2" (38 mm) tall support block.
Route 1-1/2" PVC or equivalent rigid piping between the bath and the blower motor, connecting at each previously cut end with the provided 1-1/2" couplings.
Support the piping at intervals along the length in accordance with local codes.
Use the provided longer cable to connect the blower to the user interface. The cable connector at the blower should be oriented with the flat part facing up.
Use the provided retaining clip to prevent accidental cable disconnection.
Use cable ties or other clips to support the cable.
text:
K-1446 Remote Blower Kit Installation

# Overview
- KOHLER BubbleMassage™ air baths come equipped with a coiled section of 1" flexible PVC piping between the bath and the blower motor.
- The coiled piping must remain intact to prevent back flow of water into the blower assembly.
- When relocating the blower, it is important to avoid cutting, removing, or uncoiling any part of the coiled piping.

---

# Disconnecting the Blower from the Bath

IMPORTANT: Do not cut, remove, or uncoil any part of the coiled piping.

- Cut the middle of the 1-1/2" PVC pipe located between the tee and the union nut.
- Disconnect and remove the cable between the blower and the user interface.
- Cut the straps holding the blower motor to the support board on the bath.

---

# Reconnecting the Blower at the Remote Location

Note: Locate the blower motor within 15' (4.6 m) of the bath, with no more than six direction changes in the piping.

Note: The blower motor must be oriented horizontally, and installed to a support block no lower than the original mounted height relative to the bath.

- At the new location, mount the blower on a minimum 1-1/2" (38 mm) tall support block.
- Route 1-1/2" PVC or equivalent rigid piping between the bath and the blower motor, connecting at each previously cut end with the provided 1-1/2" couplings.
- Support the piping at intervals along the length in accordance with local codes.
- Use the provided longer cable to connect the blower to the user interface. The cable connector at the blower should be oriented with the flat part facing up.
- Use the provided retaining clip to prevent accidental cable disconnection.
- Use cable ties or other clips to support the cable.

title: Whirlpool - ProFlex® Jet Removal
issue_description:
Jet removal is not necessary for regular whirlpool maintenance. However, you may want to change the color of the jet trim in your whirlpool. This can be done with the KOHLER® jet removal tool included with new jets.

---
corrective_actions: NOTE: A special tool is provided with replacement jets and with trim kits. This tool allows you to remove the jets from the whirlpool. NOTE: During jet removal, the nozzle must be pointed up or the tool will slip off.
Position the jet ball nozzle so it is pointing upward.
Insert the removal tool, hooked end up, into the opening of the jet and hook the inside top of the nozzle.
Grasp the tool firmly and place your thumb against the whirlpool wall.
Pull steadily on the tool until the jet assembly pulls free from the hole. Be careful not to lose the O-ring. ---
NOTE: To allow smooth rotation and proper operation of the jet, the O-ring must be: (1) correctly positioned, (2) lubricated, and (3) in good condition.
Install the O-ring onto the first shoulder of the jet.
Using the silicone lube packet (provided), lubricate the O-ring to prevent noisy operation of the jet.
Carefully insert the jet into the housing, then lightly push and rotate the jet until it snaps into position. Do not force the jet.
Verify the jet is installed correctly. The jet should turn smoothly both clockwise and counterclockwise. Remove and reinstall, if necessary.
text:
Whirlpool - ProFlex® Jet Removal

# Overview
Jet removal is not necessary for regular whirlpool maintenance. However, you may want to change the color of the jet trim in your whirlpool. This can be done with the KOHLER® jet removal tool included with new jets.

---

# Removing the Jet

NOTE: A special tool is provided with replacement jets and with trim kits. This tool allows you to remove the jets from the whirlpool.

NOTE: During jet removal, the nozzle must be pointed up or the tool will slip off.

- Position the jet ball nozzle so it is pointing upward.
- Insert the removal tool, hooked end up, into the opening of the jet and hook the inside top of the nozzle.
- Grasp the tool firmly and place your thumb against the whirlpool wall.
- Pull steadily on the tool until the jet assembly pulls free from the hole. Be careful not to lose the O-ring.

---

# Reinstalling the Jet

NOTE: To allow smooth rotation and proper operation of the jet, the O-ring must be: (1) correctly positioned, (2) lubricated, and (3) in good condition.

- Install the O-ring onto the first shoulder of the jet.
- Using the silicone lube packet (provided), lubricate the O-ring to prevent noisy operation of the jet.
- Carefully insert the jet into the housing, then lightly push and rotate the jet until it snaps into position. Do not force the jet.
- Verify the jet is installed correctly. The jet should turn smoothly both clockwise and counterclockwise. Remove and reinstall, if necessary.

title: Vikrell® Bathing Fixture With Dry-Block™ Seal Leak Repair
issue_description:
- Repair front corner leaks in Vikrell bathing fixtures with Dry-Block seal.

---
corrective_actions: Safety Glasses
100% Silicone Sealant
Fine Grit Sandpaper
Conventional Woodworking Tools and Materials NOTE: Use colored 100% silicone sealant to ensure against leaks. Use of latex, acrylic, or other caulks is not recommended. ---
Cut away the damaged wall material around the seam between the bath and side wall. The cutout should be at least 2” (51 mm) wide and 4” (102 mm) long.
Clean the surface of the seam with fine grit sandpaper to ensure a good bond with the sealant. ---
NOTE: Make sure that the seam is clean and dry before applying sealant.
Apply a continuous bead of 100% silicone sealant to the first 4" (102 mm) of the seam, across the front edge of the wall panel, and up 1" (25 mm) of the tile flange as shown.
Replace the wall material and restore the wall finish.
text:
Vikrell® Bathing Fixture With Dry-Block™ Seal Leak Repair

# Overview
- Repair front corner leaks in Vikrell bathing fixtures with Dry-Block seal.

---

# Recommended Tools

- Safety Glasses
- 100% Silicone Sealant
- Fine Grit Sandpaper
- Conventional Woodworking Tools and Materials

NOTE: Use colored 100% silicone sealant to ensure against leaks. Use of latex, acrylic, or other caulks is not recommended.

---

# Remove the Damaged Material

- Cut away the damaged wall material around the seam between the bath and side wall. The cutout should be at least 2” (51 mm) wide and 4” (102 mm) long.
- Clean the surface of the seam with fine grit sandpaper to ensure a good bond with the sealant.

---

# Apply Sealant and Replace the Material

NOTE: Make sure that the seam is clean and dry before applying sealant.

- Apply a continuous bead of 100% silicone sealant to the first 4" (102 mm) of the seam, across the front edge of the wall panel, and up 1" (25 mm) of the tile flange as shown.
- Replace the wall material and restore the wall finish.

title: Antique Ball & Claw Bath Leg Change
corrective_actions: Effectivity Date: 5/6/14
An engineering change was made to the K-102 Antique ball and claw bath legs.
The old leg had a straight attachment hole.
The new leg has an angled (9°) attachment hole.
The change affects how the legs are installed to the K-100 Birthday® bath. ---
The K-102 legs were difficult to install to the K-100 bath, resulting in improper assembly to the bath.
Improper leg installation can compromise the stability of the bath and legs assembly. ---

NOTICE: Refer to the installation guide packed with your K-100 or K-102 product for specific leg assembly instructions. IMPORTANT! To ensure proper bath support, the load lug on the bath must rest on the flat interior surface of the leg.
Verify which leg design you have to determine installation using a bevelled washer or two flat washers.
Old leg (straight hole): install to the bath using the #3/8-16 UNC-2B fastening bolt and the beveled washer provided with the product.
New leg (angled hole): install to the bath using the #3/8-16 UNC-2B fastening bolt and two flat washers provided with the product.
text:
Antique Ball & Claw Bath Leg Change

# Leg Part Change
Effectivity Date: 5/6/14

- An engineering change was made to the K-102 Antique ball and claw bath legs.
- The old leg had a straight attachment hole.
- The new leg has an angled (9°) attachment hole.
- The change affects how the legs are installed to the K-100 Birthday® bath.

---

# Reason for the Change

- The K-102 legs were difficult to install to the K-100 bath, resulting in improper assembly to the bath.
- Improper leg installation can compromise the stability of the bath and legs assembly.

---

# Leg Assembly to the Bath

NOTICE: Refer to the installation guide packed with your K-100 or K-102 product for specific leg assembly instructions.

IMPORTANT! To ensure proper bath support, the load lug on the bath must rest on the flat interior surface of the leg.

- Verify which leg design you have to determine installation using a bevelled washer or two flat washers.
- Old leg (straight hole): install to the bath using the #3/8-16 UNC-2B fastening bolt and the beveled washer provided with the product.
- New leg (angled hole): install to the bath using the #3/8-16 UNC-2B fastening bolt and two flat washers provided with the product.

corrective_actions: To open and close the drain:

Pull up on the handle until it "clicks" twice.

title: Freestanding Baths - Disassembly for Servicing
issue_description:
Kohler Co. recommends that their freestanding baths be installed with access from below. In cases where access from below has been provided, the following disassembly procedure is not needed.

If access from below was not provided for your freestanding bath installation, follow the steps below to disassemble and remove the bath from the shroud for any servicing required.

NOTE: Two people are required to lift and move this product.

NOTE: The drain and overflow for your product may differ in appearance from the one shown. The disassembly and removal procedures remain the same.

---
corrective_actions: NOTE: Retain all the components for reassembly.
Remove the drain and overflow covers.
Loosen and remove the overflow flange screws, and remove the overflow flange.
Turn the drain strainer counterclockwise to loosen and remove.
Unplug the blower (some models) and any connections.
With help, carefully lift the bath up and away from the shroud.
Carefully set the bath on the floor to service as needed. ---
Follow the installation instructions to reinstall.
text:
Freestanding Baths - Disassembly for Servicing

# Overview
Kohler Co. recommends that their freestanding baths be installed with access from below. In cases where access from below has been provided, the following disassembly procedure is not needed.

If access from below was not provided for your freestanding bath installation, follow the steps below to disassemble and remove the bath from the shroud for any servicing required.

NOTE: Two people are required to lift and move this product.

NOTE: The drain and overflow for your product may differ in appearance from the one shown. The disassembly and removal procedures remain the same.

---

# Disassembly

NOTE: Retain all the components for reassembly.

- Remove the drain and overflow covers.
- Loosen and remove the overflow flange screws, and remove the overflow flange.
- Turn the drain strainer counterclockwise to loosen and remove.

- Unplug the blower (some models) and any connections.
- With help, carefully lift the bath up and away from the shroud.
- Carefully set the bath on the floor to service as needed.

---

# Re-Installation

issue_description:
The two-way diverter valve, model K-9530, utilizes four ports to allow the valve to be installed in a deck mount or wall mount installation application.

Three ports of the valve are 3/4”-14 NPSM thread. The smaller 1/2”-14 NPSM thread port is intended for a handshower only. Please review the [installation instructions](https://www.us.kohler.com/webassets/kpna/catalog/pdf/en/12298132.pdf) for installation specific plumbing diagrams.

The valve was introduced in 1994, before PEX or PVC fittings were introduced into the plumbing industry, and thus maintains the NPSM thread.

title: Sterling Accord Seated Showers and Shower Curtains
issue_description:
The Accord Vikrell Seated Shower has a gap between the end of the seat and the inside threshold of approximately 1 inch. A shower curtain could fit in this gap. If the shower curtain runs longer, it could be pinched between the seat and the threshold.

During testing, it was discovered that a longer, pinched shower curtain may be better.  If the shower curtain is not long enough, during showering, the water may run down the front angled side of the seat and kick the shower curtain outward causing water to exit the shower and get on the floor. If it is pinched, the shower curtain will stay in place and prevent water from exiting the shower.

title: Devonshire® and Portrait® Whirlpool Jets
issue_description:
Jet removal is not necessary for regular whirlpool maintenance. However, you may want to change the color of the jet trim in your whirlpool. This can be done with the KOHLER® jet trim tool included with new jets.

---
corrective_actions: The jet removal tool has a hook each end.
The small hook is used to catch the back edge of the center part of the jet, called the "eyeball."
The large hook is intended to wrap around your finger for leverage.
Insert the small hook into the jet. It may take a few tries to properly hook the eyeball and keep it in place.
Once you feel the hook catch on the jet, pull on the jet firmly to un-snap it from the flange. You may need to use some downward pressure to keep the hook in place as you pull.
Once the eyeball and sleeve are removed, the adjustable trim ring will pull off.
text:
Devonshire® and Portrait® Whirlpool Jets

# Overview
Jet removal is not necessary for regular whirlpool maintenance. However, you may want to change the color of the jet trim in your whirlpool. This can be done with the KOHLER® jet trim tool included with new jets.

---

# Removing the Jet

- The jet removal tool has a hook each end.
- The small hook is used to catch the back edge of the center part of the jet, called the "eyeball."
- The large hook is intended to wrap around your finger for leverage.

- Insert the small hook into the jet. It may take a few tries to properly hook the eyeball and keep it in place.
- Once you feel the hook catch on the jet, pull on the jet firmly to un-snap it from the flange. You may need to use some downward pressure to keep the hook in place as you pull.
- Once the eyeball and sleeve are removed, the adjustable trim ring will pull off.

title: Elevance® Rising Wall Bath - Proper Operation
corrective_actions: Follow the steps below to verify that the bath is functioning properly. Fill the Bath
With the door down, close the toe-tap drain.

Turn the water ON and check the temperature. NOTE: The back wall drain will remain open, only allowing the water level to rise to approximately 4" (102 mm). This allows the bather to set the desired water temperature before beginning to fill the bath.
Once the desired temperature is reached, raise the door. The door seals will inflate and the back wall drain will close, allowing the bath to fill.
Turn the water OFF. IMPORTANT! If the level sensors are not submerged in water within 2 minutes of raising the door, the back wall drain will open, draining the water from the bath. Drain the Bath
Tap the door switch once. The back wall drain will open and the bath will drain.
Open the toe-tap drain to fully drain the bath. IMPORTANT! The water level must drop below the level sensors before the door seals will deflate, allowing the doors to open.
Allow the water to drain below the level sensors and wait for the door seals to deflate.
Squeeze the door handle then lower the door.
Repeat the test procedure four to five times to ensure the bath is operating correctly. ---
When filling the bath, some water will drain through the accumulator drain hose and route to the drip tray. It is normal to hear a trickle of water during or immediately after filling the bath.
After the door is raised while the door seal is inflating, you will hear the compressor run for up to 90 seconds.
If the door is fully raised for more than 20 minutes and there is no water in the bath, the seals will automatically deflate.
When the water level falls below the sensors, the door seals will deflate. You will hear the solenoid valve open and expel air.
The bather’s movement or excessive splashing can cause the water to run over the inflated seals; this water will be captured in the drip tray.
Water that has collected on the seals during use will drain to the drip tray as they deflate.
text:
Elevance® Rising Wall Bath - Proper Operation

# Test for Proper Function
Follow the steps below to verify that the bath is functioning properly.

Fill the Bath

- With the door down, close the toe-tap drain.
- Turn the water ON and check the temperature.

NOTE: The back wall drain will remain open, only allowing the water level to rise to approximately 4" (102 mm). This allows the bather to set the desired water temperature before beginning to fill the bath.

- Once the desired temperature is reached, raise the door. The door seals will inflate and the back wall drain will close, allowing the bath to fill.
- Turn the water OFF.

IMPORTANT! If the level sensors are not submerged in water within 2 minutes of raising the door, the back wall drain will open, draining the water from the bath.

Drain the Bath

- Tap the door switch once. The back wall drain will open and the bath will drain.
- Open the toe-tap drain to fully drain the bath.

IMPORTANT! The water level must drop below the level sensors before the door seals will deflate, allowing the doors to open.

- Allow the water to drain below the level sensors and wait for the door seals to deflate.
- Squeeze the door handle then lower the door.
- Repeat the test procedure four to five times to ensure the bath is operating correctly.

---

# Normal Occurrences During Operation

- When filling the bath, some water will drain through the accumulator drain hose and route to the drip tray. It is normal to hear a trickle of water during or immediately after filling the bath.
- After the door is raised while the door seal is inflating, you will hear the compressor run for up to 90 seconds.
- If the door is fully raised for more than 20 minutes and there is no water in the bath, the seals will automatically deflate.
- When the water level falls below the sensors, the door seals will deflate. You will hear the solenoid valve open and expel air.
- The bather’s movement or excessive splashing can cause the water to run over the inflated seals; this water will be captured in the drip tray.
- Water that has collected on the seals during use will drain to the drip tray as they deflate.

title: BubbleMassage™ Air Bath with Bask™ Wiring for 240 V
corrective_actions: Between late 2013 and early 2014, some BubbleMassage baths with Bask heater were shipped with incorrect wiring for 240 V installation.
The Bask power supply on these baths came equipped with a junction box and a 110 V power cord with plug.
For installation to 240 V service, the Bask power supply must be disconnected from the Bask junction box and wired directly into the blower junction box.
The installation instructions packed with the product may not show wiring connections for 240 V installation. ---

WARNING: Risk of electric shock. A qualified electrician should complete or rework the electrical service to the BubbleMassage bath. WARNING: Risk of electric shock. Disconnect power before servicing. NOTE: Before replacing components or dispatching a Kohler Co. Authorized Service Representative:
The model number and electrical rating must be verified. These are listed on the label located near the blower assembly.
An access panel must be present to allow the blower and heater components to be serviced. The panel must be a minimum of 20" (508 mm) in width and 15" (381 mm) in height.
Dedicated 240 V electrical service must be properly connected to the blower junction box. The junction box is located next to the blower, mounted to a board above the controller. ---
Disconnect the power supply.
Remove the Bask power supply cord (top cord) and strain relief from the Bask power cord junction box by disconnecting the wires from the terminal connectors inside the box.
Rewire the Bask power supply cord into the blower junction box. Refer to the wiring diagram to connect the power supply wires to the appropriate terminals inside the box.
Make sure the strain relief is attached to the cord where it enters the junction box.
Confirm that the electrical installation was properly completed by verifying that the BubbleMassage bath with Bask is operating as described in the Installation and Care Guide.
text:
BubbleMassage™ Air Bath with Bask™ Wiring for 240 V

# Wiring Discrepancy for Some 240 V Models

- Between late 2013 and early 2014, some BubbleMassage baths with Bask heater were shipped with incorrect wiring for 240 V installation.
- The Bask power supply on these baths came equipped with a junction box and a 110 V power cord with plug.
- For installation to 240 V service, the Bask power supply must be disconnected from the Bask junction box and wired directly into the blower junction box.
- The installation instructions packed with the product may not show wiring connections for 240 V installation.

---

# Important Information Before Rewiring for 240 V Service

WARNING: Risk of electric shock. A qualified electrician should complete or rework the electrical service to the BubbleMassage bath.

WARNING: Risk of electric shock. Disconnect power before servicing.

NOTE: Before replacing components or dispatching a Kohler Co. Authorized Service Representative:

- The model number and electrical rating must be verified. These are listed on the label located near the blower assembly.
- An access panel must be present to allow the blower and heater components to be serviced. The panel must be a minimum of 20" (508 mm) in width and 15" (381 mm) in height.
- Dedicated 240 V electrical service must be properly connected to the blower junction box. The junction box is located next to the blower, mounted to a board above the controller.

---

# Rewiring for 240 V Service

- Disconnect the power supply.
- Remove the Bask power supply cord (top cord) and strain relief from the Bask power cord junction box by disconnecting the wires from the terminal connectors inside the box.
- Rewire the Bask power supply cord into the blower junction box. Refer to the wiring diagram to connect the power supply wires to the appropriate terminals inside the box.
- Make sure the strain relief is attached to the cord where it enters the junction box.
- Confirm that the electrical installation was properly completed by verifying that the BubbleMassage bath with Bask is operating as described in the Installation and Care Guide.

title: Sterling Vikrell and Severe Cold Conditions
issue_description:
As part of the product development process, Sterling has conducted extreme temperature testing on Sterling Vikrell bathing and showering products. Testing involves cycling the product between -40 F and +160 F five times and then inspecting for damage. Our Vikrell products pass this test.

title: Adjust Bubble Massage Blower Speed
issue_description:
Blower speed on a Bubble Massage bath can be changed by using the keypad's up and down buttons. If the blower speed does not change, please refer to the information below.

Ensure that your Bubble Massage bath is a Kohler product. Refer to "[Identifying Your Bath or Whirlpool Model](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-bath-or-whirlpool-model) " to locate the model number of your bath.

---
causes: Ensure that you are pressing the "ON" button and not the "purge button."  Pushing the purge button will cause the system to start but not adjust.

Kohler designed the Bubble Massage to ensure that air flows across the entire bath, even at the lowest setting, lowest available voltage (107 Volts) and with the deepest bath available. That condition limits the range of our blower speed.

In smaller bathrooms or in environments where tiles or solid surface materials are used, the noise generated by a Bubble Massage is louder than a whirlpool unit. In these environments, it becomes difficult to notice the change in the speed of the blower. How to Identify the Issue: 1 Fill bath up to the overflow. 2 Start the Bubble Massage. 3 Open the access panel. 4 While listening to the blower (may require assistance from a second person), press and hold the "Low Speed" button on the keypad. 5 Notice that the blower, not the bubbles, is making less noise. 6 With the bath filled to the overflow, a decrease in bubble intensity should be noticeable. Recommended Action:

In most cases, the blower is operating correctly. Sending a new blower, controller or keypad will not resolve the issue. Instead, it may belay the resolution or incur additional cost from unnecessary repairs.
Use a multi-meter to measure amperage variation while pressing the low/high speed buttons. ---
corrective_actions: Kohler products require either 110V or 220V. Numerous occurrences have been documented in which the wrong voltage was supplied, causing issues with product performance. How to Identify the Issue: 1 Locate the label new the blower motor. 2 Identify the model number and required electrical rating.
If rating is 110V, plug a standard electric appliance, like a lamp or hair dryer, into the outlet to confirm that there is power.

If rating is 220V, use a voltmeter to measure the supply voltage for your product. Recommended Action: If the current supply voltage is not compatible with the bath, contact a licensed electrician to install the correct voltage.
text:
Adjust Bubble Massage Blower Speed

Blower speed on a Bubble Massage bath can be changed by using the keypad's up and down buttons. If the blower speed does not change, please refer to the information below.

Ensure that your Bubble Massage bath is a Kohler product. Refer to "[Identifying Your Bath or Whirlpool Model](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/identifying-your-bath-or-whirlpool-model) " to locate the model number of your bath.

---

# Low Setting on Blower Doesn't Seem Low Enough - Probable Causes

- Ensure that you are pressing the "ON" button and not the "purge button."  Pushing the purge button will cause the system to start but not adjust.
- Kohler designed the Bubble Massage to ensure that air flows across the entire bath, even at the lowest setting, lowest available voltage (107 Volts) and with the deepest bath available. That condition limits the range of our blower speed.
- In smaller bathrooms or in environments where tiles or solid surface materials are used, the noise generated by a Bubble Massage is louder than a whirlpool unit. In these environments, it becomes difficult to notice the change in the speed of the blower.

How to Identify the Issue:

1
Fill bath up to the overflow.

2
Start the Bubble Massage.

3
Open the access panel.

4
While listening to the blower (may require assistance from a second person), press and hold the "Low Speed" button on the keypad.

5
Notice that the blower, not the bubbles, is making less noise.

6
With the bath filled to the overflow, a decrease in bubble intensity should be noticeable.

Recommended Action:

- In most cases, the blower is operating correctly. Sending a new blower, controller or keypad will not resolve the issue. Instead, it may belay the resolution or incur additional cost from unnecessary repairs.
- Use a multi-meter to measure amperage variation while pressing the low/high speed buttons.

---

# Supply Voltage - Confirm Compatibility
- Kohler products require either 110V or 220V. Numerous occurrences have been documented in which the wrong voltage was supplied, causing issues with product performance.

How to Identify the Issue:

1
Locate the label new the blower motor.

2
Identify the model number and required electrical rating.

- If rating is 110V, plug a standard electric appliance, like a lamp or hair dryer, into the outlet to confirm that there is power.
- If rating is 220V, use a voltmeter to measure the supply voltage for your product.

Recommended Action:

If the current supply voltage is not compatible with the bath, contact a licensed electrician to install the correct voltage.

title: Toilet Constantly Leaking or Running
issue_description:
Why is my toilet constantly leaking or running?  This troubleshooting document relates to one or two-piece toilets.

With this issue, water constantly leaks or runs from the toilet tank into the toilet bowl because the trip lever arm may be binding, water may be overflowing into the flush valve overflow, or debris may be lodged underneath the cap of the fill valve.

You will hear a constant filling or running noise coming from the toilet tank that does not stop. You may also see a slight ripple of water in the toilet bowl. If you remove the tank lid, you will notice water overflowing into the overflow of the flush valve.

Flapper style toilet (left) and canister style toilet (right)
corrective_actions: Clean the fill valve or replace the fill valve. Flapper style toilet (left) and canister style toilet (right)

Leaking or constant running is often caused by sediment or debris lodged in the cap of the fill valve preventing the water from turning off. The fill valve fills the tank and bowl with water after the toilet is flushed. text:
Toilet Constantly Leaking or Running

Why is my toilet constantly leaking or running?  This troubleshooting document relates to one or two-piece toilets. 

## Description of Issue
With this issue, water constantly leaks or runs from the toilet tank into the toilet bowl because the trip lever arm may be binding, water may be overflowing into the flush valve overflow, or debris may be lodged underneath the cap of the fill valve.

## Symptoms of Constant Leaking or Running
You will hear a constant filling or running noise coming from the toilet tank that does not stop. You may also see a slight ripple of water in the toilet bowl. If you remove the tank lid, you will notice water overflowing into the overflow of the flush valve.

Flapper style toilet (left) and canister style toilet (right)

# Corrective Actions:
- Clean the fill valve or replace the fill valve.

Flapper style toilet (left) and canister style toilet (right)

- Leaking or constant running is often caused by sediment or debris lodged in the cap of the fill valve preventing the water from turning off. The fill valve fills the tank and bowl with water after the toilet is flushed. This issue is common during new toilet installation because turning the water supply on and off can loosen sediment within the water lines. 

- Replace the fill valve if the toilet is still constantly running after flushing the fill valve. The part number of the fill valve will vary based on the toilet model number.

- This video will show you how to flush the fill valve in a KOHLER two-piece toilet in under 10 minutes.

All you will need to perform this maintenance is a plastic cup.
https://youtu.be/oD0HETCc-OQ

- This video will show you how to flush the fill valve in a KOHLER low-profile one-piece toilet in under 10 minutes.

All you will need to perform this maintenance is a plastic cup.

https://youtu.be/34h-XoCb-4o

- Adjust the trip lever chain for proper slack . The chain should have roughly one to two links of slack so the excess chain does not get caught on the trip lever arm. Remove excess chain if needed. 

- Adjust tank water level to prevent water from overfilling and running into the flush valve overflow.

- If tank water spills into the overflow but eventually stops, the tank water level will need to be adjusted. Reference "[Adjust the Amount of Water in a Toilet Tank](https://www.kohler.com/en/support/help-and-faq/adjust-the-amount-of-water-in-a-toilet-tank) ."

issue_description:

Some Kohler one-piece toilets utilize an anchor to receive the toilet seat bolt because of the toilet design. The anchor can receive a 1/4-20" UNC bolt thread pattern.

Because of the different sizes, to install a wood toilet seat to a toilet that utilizes anchors, simply purchase hardware kit 1104015. The hardware kit comes with the appropriate size bolts to connect a wood toilet seat to an anchor toilet. The washers and nuts from the hardware kit may be discarded as they are not necessary for an toilet that utilizes anchors.

title: Weight/Load Bearing Limit for Kohler Toilets, Toilet Seats and Lavatories
issue_description:
Refer to the following information for weight/load bearing limits for KOHLER Toilets, Toilet Seats and Lavatories.

Current production KOHLER floor mounted vitreous china water closet bowls will withstand a vertical force up to 1,000 lbs. Note that there are no standards that specify a minimum load bearing capability requirement for floor mount water closets. Products met the requirements of the standard on the date the product was manufactured.

Current production KOHLER wall mounted vitreous china water closets meet the 500 lbs. minimum load bearing requirements of the ASME A112.19.2-2005/CSA B4 5.1-05 National Consensus Standards for Vitreous China Plumbing Fixtures.

Current product KOHLER wall mounted lavatories meet the 250 lbs. minimum load bearing requirements of the ASME A112.19.2-2005/CSA B45.1-05 National Consensus Standards for Vitreous China Plumbing Fixtures.

Current product KOHLER wall mounted vitreous china urinals meet the 50 lbs. minimum load bearing requirements of the ASME A112.19.2-2005/CSA B45.1-05 National Consensus Standards for Vitreous China Plumbing Fixtures.

KOHLER does not specify a weight limit on our toilet seats. These seats are designed to pass the industry standard ANSI Z124  Plastic Toilet Seat Test Requirements for residential toilet seats. This specification calls out static load tests of 300 lbs. and several dynamic tests that involve side load rocking and drop testing, which these seats have passed.

Please note that the aforementioned standards apply to current production products. The ASME Standards are not controlled by Kohler Co. and are subject to change.

(Dated 7/26/11)

# Wall Mounted Toilets

# Wall Mounted Lavatories
Current product KOHLER wall mounted lavatories meet the 250 lbs. minimum load bearing requirements of the ASME A112.19.2-2005/CSA B45.1-05 National Consensus Standards for Vitreous China Plumbing Fixtures.

Current product KOHLER wall mounted vitreous china urinals meet the 50 lbs. minimum load bearing requirements of the ASME A112.19.2-2005/CSA B45.1-05 National Consensus Standards for Vitreous China Plumbing Fixtures.

# Toilet Seats

title: How a Toilet Flushes
issue_description:
There are many toilet designs; however, most function simply through the natural forces of gravity and a change in pressure.

Typically, a toilet will consist of a tank that acts as a storage reservoir for water. Controlling the flow of water to and from the tank is accomplished by using a fill valve and a flush valve. The tank is either mounted to, or made an integral part of, the toilet bowl. At the rear of the bowl there is an outlet which leads to a large diameter curved pipe, or trapway, which carries waste material to the sanitary drainpipe.

When the toilet is not in use, a small amount of water remains in the toilet bowl because the pressure inside the bowl and the pressure inside the trapway are equal. Depressing a trip lever activates the flush cycle by opening the flush valve flapper and allowing water to feed from the tank to the bowl. Water will travel by force of gravity from the tank to the bowl though a variety of specially engineered passages.

The surge of water to the bowl quickly fills the trapway and displaces the air space within the trapway. The resulting change in pressure causes a siphon to be formed. Water and waste material are drawn though the trapway and out into the sanitary sewer line by the force of the siphon. When enough water has left the tank, the flush valve flapper closes and water flow to the bowl is suspended. As air gradually reenters the trapway, the pressure equalizes and the siphon is lost.

As soon as the water level in the tank begins to drop, a float mounted on the fill valve begins to travel downward. This downward travel activates the fill valve and initiates the refilling of the tank and the bowl with fresh water. As the tank refills, the float begins to rise with the incoming water. The fill valve shuts off when the tank water height reaches a predetermined level. Once the tank has filled sufficiently, the system is ready for another flush cycle.

This same process applies to pressure-assisted and pump toilet designs, expect that supply line water pressure or an electric pump is used to supplement the force of gravity when delivering water to the bowl. Many commercial toilets do not have tank, and use only supply line water pressure to feed water to the bowl.
